Civility and utility share this ending.
items.exampleCN: civility 与 utility 共用此词尾。

items.example: The annuitant cashed the yearly cheque.
items.exampleCN: 受益人兑现了年度支票。
他们庆祝了金婚纪念日。
两年一度的报告追踪进展。

definition_zh: 语言习得；母语习得；第二语言习得；语言学习过程
definition_en: the process by which a person comes to understand and use a language, especially without formal teaching
core_image: 一个孩子坐在餐桌旁，把大人们说的碎片一句句收进自己的小盒子，慢慢能拼成整句。
scene: 一个孩子在异国幼儿园待了一年，没有上过语法课，却能跟同伴讨价还价。 After a year in a foreign kindergarten, the child's language acquisition outpaced every adult's textbook study.
sceneCN: 这里 language acquisition 指「在自然接触中逐步获得语言能力的过程」（第 1 个义项：不经正式教学而掌握语言的整体过程）；句意为孩子在异国幼儿园一年，语言习得的速度超过了成年人按课本学习。可辨识物件：幼儿园院子、同伴、孩子、玩具。

pos.zh: 语言习得；母语习得；第二语言习得

collocations.zh: 母语习得；第一语言习得

senses.title: Gaining a language as a whole
senses.titleCN: 整体获得一种语言能力
senses.definition: the process by which someone comes to understand and produce a language, whether at home or in a new community
senses.definitionCN: 某人逐步理解并产出一种语言的过程，无论在家庭还是在新社群中
senses.example: After a year in a foreign kindergarten, the child's language acquisition outpaced every adult's textbook study.
senses.exampleCN: 在异国幼儿园待了一年后，孩子的语言习得速度超过了成年人按课本学习。
senses.why: The phrase joins the whole system to the act of coming to have it, so it names a process rather than a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把整个语言系统与「逐渐拥有它」的动作连在一起，因此指一种过程，而非一堂课。

senses.title: Learning a first language at home
senses.titleCN: 在家庭环境中习得母语
senses.definition: the natural development of a first language in early childhood through everyday interaction
senses.definitionCN: 幼儿期通过日常互动自然发展出第一语言
senses.example: First language acquisition happens without a syllabus or a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 母语习得没有教学大纲，也没有老师。
senses.why: The first language is acquired before schooling, so the general phrase is narrowed by the word first.
senses.whyCN: 第一语言在上学之前就已获得，因此「第一」一词把通用短语收窄到这一情形。

senses.title: Learning a later language in use
senses.titleCN: 在使用环境中习得第二语言
senses.definition: the development of a second or additional language through exposure and interaction rather than only through instruction
senses.definitionCN: 通过接触与互动、而非仅靠课堂教学发展出第二或更多语言
senses.example: Second language acquisition research asks why some learners stop improving.
senses.exampleCN: 第二语言习得研究追问为什么有些学习者会停止进步。
senses.why: The word second marks the later language, and acquisition marks learning by use rather than by rule memorization.
senses.whyCN: 「第二」标出较晚学习的语言，「习得」标出靠使用而非背规则来学习。

senses.title: Absorbing a language without lessons
senses.titleCN: 不经课堂而自然吸收语言
senses.definition: the uptake of a language from daily exposure, with little conscious study of grammar
senses.definitionCN: 从日常接触中吸收语言，几乎不有意识学习语法
senses.example: Her Spanish came from acquisition, not from evening classes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的西班牙语来自自然习得，而不是夜校课程。
senses.why: This sense draws the line between acquisition and learning that language teaching theory often insists on.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项划出「习得」与「学习」的界线，语言教学理论常强调这条线。

senses.title: A child's growing command of speech
senses.definition: the sequence of stages by which a child moves from first sounds to full sentences
senses.definitionCN: 儿童从最初的发音走向完整句子的阶段序列
senses.example: Child language acquisition moves from one word to many before grammar appears.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童语言习得先从一个词走向许多词，然后才出现语法。
senses.why: Researchers name the whole developmental sequence with the same phrase because each stage is part of one gaining.
senses.whyCN: 研究者用同一个短语命名整段发展序列，因为每个阶段都属于同一次获得。

senses.title: Growing up with two languages
senses.titleCN: 在双语环境中习得两种语言
senses.definition: the simultaneous or successive development of two languages in a young learner
senses.definitionCN: 年幼学习者在同一时期或先后发展出两种语言
senses.example: Bilingual acquisition can produce different strengths in each language.
senses.exampleCN: 双语习得可能在两种语言上形成不同的强项。
senses.why: The phrase is extended by the word bilingual, but the underlying process of gaining a system remains the same.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语被「双语的」一词扩展，但获得一个语言系统的底层过程并未改变。

senses.title: The research field that studies it
senses.titleCN: 研究语言习得的学科领域
senses.definition: the academic study of how languages are acquired by children and adults
senses.definitionCN: 研究儿童与成人如何习得语言的学术领域
senses.example: Language acquisition draws on psychology, linguistics and education.
senses.exampleCN: 语言习得研究借助心理学、语言学与教育学。
senses.why: As with other processes, the name of the activity becomes the name of the field that investigates it.
senses.whyCN: 与其他过程一样，活动的名称也成为研究该活动的学科名称。

senses.title: Gaining one specific part of a language
senses.titleCN: 习得语言的某一具体成分
senses.definition: the acquisition of a particular component such as vocabulary, a sound or a grammatical pattern
senses.definitionCN: 对词汇、某个语音或某种语法模式等具体成分的习得
senses.example: Vocabulary acquisition slows once a learner stops reading widely.
senses.exampleCN: 学习者一旦停止广泛阅读，词汇习得就会变慢。
senses.why: The whole process can be named for one of its parts, so the phrase also covers learning a single layer of language.
senses.whyCN: 整个流程可以用它的某一部分来命名，因此这个短语也涵盖学习语言的某一层。

intro.en: Language acquisition joins a noun carried from Old French to English with a Latin noun of action from acquirere, to get in addition.
intro.cn: language acquisition 把一个经古法语进入英语的名词，与来自拉丁 acquirere「额外取得」的动作名词连在一起。

items.en: Lingua meant tongue and language. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed form, and no single source is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头与语言。其更早来源一般认为是重构形式，学界并未就单一来源达成一致。

items.en: Acquirere meant to get in addition, from a prefix meaning to or toward and quaerere, to seek. The image is of seeking something and adding it to what one already has.
items.cn: acquirere 意为「额外取得」，由表示「朝向」的前缀与 quaerere「寻找」构成；意象是寻得某物并把它加进已有的东西。

items.en: The action noun acquisitio passed through Old French acquisition into English, where it first named the obtaining of property or knowledge.
items.cn: 动作名词 acquisitio 经古法语 acquisition 进入英语，最初指获得财产或知识。

items.en: Language and acquisition were joined in learned writing, and the pair named the gaining of a language system rather than the gaining of a single word.
items.cn: language 与 acquisition 在学术写作中被组合起来，这一搭配指获得整个语言系统，而非获得单个词。

items.en: The phrase became a standard term in linguistics and psychology after the mid-twentieth century, when first and second language acquisition were studied as separate questions.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶以后，这个短语成为语言学与心理学的标准术语，母语习得与第二语言习得被当作两个独立问题研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of seek and the phrase's first fixed use): the older source of quaerere is a reconstruction, and no single first citation for the full phrase is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「寻找」义的拉丁语之前来源与该短语首次固定使用）：quaerere 的更早来源属重构；整个短语没有公认的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds family members that differ in word class; group two holds names for neighbouring processes.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中词性不同的词；第二组是相邻过程的名称。

entries.definition: The act of obtaining something, from property to skills; language acquisition narrows it to one kind of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物的动作，从财产到技能；language acquisition 把它收窄到一种获得。

entries.definition: To obtain or come to have; the verb can take a language, a habit or a company as its object.
entries.definitionCN: 获得或逐渐拥有；这个动词可以带语言、习惯或公司作宾语。

entries.definition: Eager to possess things; it describes a person's attitude, not the process of learning a language.
entries.definitionCN: 渴望占有物品的；它描述人的态度，而非学习语言的过程。

entries.definition: Gaining knowledge or skill by study or experience; acquisition is often reserved for uptake without formal teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 通过学习或经验获得知识或技能；acquisition 常专指不经正式教学的吸收。

entries.definition: Gaining a language through lessons and deliberate practice; it contrasts with acquisition in teaching theory.
entries.definitionCN: 通过课程与刻意练习获得语言；在教学理论中与习得相对。

entries.definition: The growth of language ability over time, often used for children; it stresses change rather than the act of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 语言能力随时间成长，常用于儿童；强调变化而非获得动作。

entries.definition: The condition of using two languages; it is the result, while acquisition is the process that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 使用两种语言的状态；它是结果，而习得是产生它的过程。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write; it is one outcome of language acquisition in a literate society.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力；在有文字的社会中，它是语言习得的一项结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the tongue root, the seeking root and the child at the table.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「舌头」词根、「寻找」词根，以及餐桌旁的孩子。

normal.en: Language goes back to a Latin word for tongue; acquisition goes back to a verb meaning to seek and add.
normal.cn: language 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「舌头」的词；acquisition 可追溯到意为「寻找并增添」的动词。

normal.en: The contrast with learning is the key: acquisition happens by use, learning by study.
normal.cn: 与「学习」的对比是关键：习得靠使用，学习靠研读。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: first language acquisition, second language acquisition, child language acquisition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分支：母语习得、第二语言习得、儿童语言习得。

normal.en: The same verb appears in acquire and acquisitive, one about gaining and one about wanting to gain.
normal.cn: 同一个动词还出现在 acquire 与 acquisitive 中，一个关于获得，一个关于想要获得。

normal.en: A child in a new playground learns the local words without a textbook, which is acquisition in the plainest form.
normal.cn: 孩子在新操场学会当地词语而不靠课本，这是最朴素的习得。

abstract.en: Picture a cup placed under a tap and filled drop by drop, with no one measuring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子放在水龙头下，一滴一滴装满，没有人计量。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that needs only soil and time, not a written plan, to become a tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子只需要土壤与时间，不需要书面计划，就能长成树。

abstract.en: Picture a language entering a child through the ears and leaving through the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一种语言从耳朵进入孩子，又从嘴巴出来。

examples.en: Second language acquisition is faster when learners hear the language every day.
examples.cn: 学习者每天都能听到该语言时，第二语言习得更快。

examples.en: The study compared language acquisition in deaf children exposed to sign from birth.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了从出生起接触手语的聋童的语言习得。

examples.en: Grammatical accuracy often arrives later than vocabulary in language acquisition.
examples.cn: 在语言习得中，语法准确往往比词汇来得更晚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 语言不是背来的，是像捡东西一样一点点「寻到并收进自己的袋子」→ 语言习得

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 入英语为 language；拉丁 acquirere「额外取得」= ad-（朝向）+ quaerere（寻找），动作名词 acquisitio 经古法语 acquisition 入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gaining: a person comes to have a language by use rather than by formal study, and the same phrase covers first, second, childhood, bilingual, partial and researched versions of that gaining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次获得展开：一个人靠使用而非正式研读逐渐拥有一种语言；同一个短语涵盖母语、第二语言、儿童、双语、部分成分以及被研究的各种获得情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child filling a small box with overheard phrases until whole sentences fit together.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子把听来的短语收进一只小盒子，直到整句能拼在一起。

branches.en: THE WHOLE GAIN: language arrives by exposure, with no syllabus directing it.
branches.cn: 整体获得：语言靠接触到来，没有大纲指挥。

branches.en: THE FIRST HOME: the earliest language is gained before any classroom exists.
branches.cn: 第一个家：最早的语言在任何课堂出现之前就已获得。

branches.en: THE LATER LANGUAGE: a second system is added while the first stays in place.
branches.cn: 较晚的语言：第二个系统被加上去，第一个仍在原处。

branches.en: THE CHILD AND THE PAIR: development unfolds in stages, sometimes in two languages at once.
branches.cn: 儿童与成对：发展按阶段展开，有时两种语言同时进行。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND THE PART: the process becomes a discipline, and a single layer can be named alone.
branches.cn: 领域与部分：过程成为学科，单一层面也可单独命名。

intro.en: The phrase combines a noun from the tongue family with a noun from the seeking family; both have wide English families of their own.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「舌头」词族中的名词与「寻找」词族中的名词组合起来；两者各自都有庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, lingual and linguistics; Latin acquirere gives acquire, acquisition, acquisitive and acquirer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 衍生 language、lingual 与 linguistics；拉丁 acquirere 衍生 acquire、acquisition、acquisitive 与 acquirer。

items.structure: Latin lingua through Old French langage
items.meaning: a system of speech or signs
items.example: Language is acquired before it is described.
items.exampleCN: 语言在被描述之前就已被习得。

items.meaning: to get or come to have
items.exampleCN: 儿童先获得语音，再获得词语。

items.meaning: the act or result of getting something
items.example: The acquisition of syntax takes years.
The acquisitive firm bought three rivals.
items.exampleCN: 这家热衷收购的公司买下了三家对手。

items.example: The acquirer kept the smaller firm's name.
items.exampleCN: 收购方保留了小公司的名称。

items.example: Acquired habits are hard to unlearn.
items.exampleCN: 已获得的习惯难以改掉。

items.example: Acquiring a language changes how one listens.
items.exampleCN: 习得一种语言会改变一个人倾听的方式。

items.example: Linguistic ability varies widely at age three.
items.exampleCN: 三岁时的语言能力差异很大。

items.example: Bilingual children switch codes with ease.
items.exampleCN: 双语儿童能轻松切换语言。

definition_zh: 成就；完成；才艺；修养
definition_en: something successfully done, the act of finishing it, or a skill gained through training
core_image: 墙上挂着一张完成证书，旁边还摆着练习多年的乐器
scene: 老人把年轻时的奖状、修好的收音机和自学的吉他照片一起摆在书架上。 Her chief accomplishment was teaching herself three languages.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplishment 是「成就」（第 1 个义项：成功做成的事）；句意为她最大的成就是自学了三门语言。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「完成；实现」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「技艺高超的」

senses.title: Something successfully achieved
senses.definition: a result that has been achieved through effort and skill
senses.definitionCN: 经努力与技能取得的结果
senses.example: Finishing the marathon was her greatest accomplishment.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完马拉松是她最大的成就。
senses.why: The -ment ending marks a result, so accomplishment is the completed thing standing in view after the effort ends.
senses.whyCN: -ment 后缀标记结果，因此 accomplishment 是努力结束后摆在眼前的已完成之物。

senses.title: The act of completing something
senses.definition: the carrying out or finishing of a task, duty, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 任务、职责或计划的执行完毕
senses.example: The accomplishment of the treaty took another year.
senses.exampleCN: 条约的完成又花了一年。
senses.why: Here the noun names the process rather than the trophy: the filling up of a task, step by step.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指过程而非奖杯：一项任务被一步步填满。

senses.title: A learned skill or grace
senses.definition: a ability polished by training, often social or artistic
senses.definitionCN: 经训练打磨的能力，常指社交或艺术方面
senses.example: Her accomplishments included watercolour painting and fluent Italian.
senses.exampleCN: 她的才艺包括水彩画和流利的意大利语。
senses.why: In older polite society, a person's accomplishments were the skills that completed a good education.
senses.whyCN: 在旧时上流社会，一个人的 accomplishments 是使良好教育「完整」的那些技艺。

intro.en: Accomplishment adds the result suffix -ment to the verb accomplish, so it names what a completed effort leaves behind.
intro.cn: accomplishment 在动词 accomplish 上加结果后缀 -ment，指完成努力后留下的东西。

items.en: plere meant 'to fill', the root of complete.
items.cn: plere 意为「填」，是 complete 的词根。

items.en: complere meant 'to fill up, finish'.
items.cn: complere 意为「填满、完成」。

items.en: acomplir meant 'to fulfil or carry out'.
items.cn: acomplir 意为「履行、完成」。

items.en: English formed the verb, then the -ment noun.
items.cn: 英语先构成动词，再加 -ment 构成名词。

items.en: The plural accomplishments named polite skills in education.
items.cn: 复数 accomplishments 在十七世纪指教育中的文雅技艺。

items.en: Modern usage stresses achievement and a sense of accomplishment.
items.cn: 现代用法强调成就与成就感。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb and its participle; the second gathers words for achievements and skills.
note.cn: 第一组收动词与其分词；第二组收表示成就与技艺的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to complete or achieve.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成、实现」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a skilled performer or writer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A partner in crime, a common spelling trap.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯」，常见拼写陷阱。

entries.definition: Something important done through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就」，经努力做成的重要之事。

entries.definition: An impressive act requiring skill or courage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「壮举」，需要技艺或勇气。

entries.definition: An ability learned through practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「技能」，经练习获得的能力。

entries.definition: The reaching of a goal or a gained ability.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「达到；造诣」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ment result rule and the award phrases; the abstract hooks picture a certificate beside a well-used instrument.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -ment 结果名词规律与奖状搭配；抽象记忆点想象证书旁摆着一件用旧的乐器。

normal.en: Accomplishment is accomplish plus -ment, so it is the result.
normal.cn: accomplishment 是 accomplish 加 -ment，指结果。

normal.en: A sense of accomplishment is the everyday phrase for pride after effort.
normal.cn: a sense of accomplishment 是努力后自豪感的日常说法。

normal.en: The plural often means polite skills: her accomplishments.
normal.cn: 复数常指文雅技艺：her accomplishments。

normal.en: Use accomplishment for the thing done, the accomplishment of for the act.
normal.cn: 指做成之事用 accomplishment，指完成的行为用 the accomplishment of。

normal.en: The spelling has double c but a single m: a-c-c-o-m-p-l-i-s-h.
normal.cn: 拼写是双 c、单 m：a-c-c-o-m-p-l-i-s-h。

abstract.en: Picture a framed certificate above a scratched guitar.
abstract.cn: 想象镶框证书上方挂着一把划痕斑驳的吉他。

abstract.en: Picture a runner crossing a line and checking the watch.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者越过终点线看表。

abstract.en: Picture a treaty signed after a year of small steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一年小步推进后签署的条约。

examples.en: Learning to swim was a real accomplishment for him.
examples.cn: 学会游泳对他而言是真正的成就。

examples.en: The accomplishment of the bridge took four years.
examples.cn: 这座桥的建成花了四年。

examples.en: Her accomplishments include piano and fluent German.
examples.cn: 她的才艺包括钢琴和流利的德语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利什门特」——努力结束后摆在眼前的那个成果，就是成就。

root: accomplish（完成）+ -ment（结果）；核心义是「把任务填满后留下的成果」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the finished result, to the act of finishing, to the skills that complete an education.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从完成后的结果，走到完成的行为，再到使教育「完整」的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a certificate hung beside a much-used instrument
core.cn: 核心意象：挂在用旧乐器旁的证书

branches.en: The achieved result that can be pointed to.
branches.cn: 可以指认的完成结果。

branches.en: The process of carrying a duty to its end.
branches.cn: 把职责做到尽头的过程。

branches.en: A trained ability that rounds out a person.
branches.cn: 使一个人更完整的受训能力。

branches.en: The trophy and the process share one noun.
branches.cn: 成果与过程共用同一个名词。

branches.en: A skill can itself be the achievement.
branches.cn: 技艺本身就可以是成就。

intro.en: The noun is the -ment result form of the filling verb, and its family keeps the verb and participle.
intro.cn: 这个名词是「填满」动词的 -ment 结果形式，词族保留动词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin complere is the ancestor behind the verb, and -ment reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 complere 是该动词背后的祖先，-ment 经法语进入英语。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」

definition_zh: 证据的；可作证据的；证据性的；（语言学）示证的
definition_en: relating to evidence, or able to serve as evidence
core_image: 一叠贴着编号的证据袋被摊开，旁边白板上画着信息来源的推断路径
scene: 语言学家在白板上画出信息来源的标记，说明有些语言用专门词尾交代消息从哪来。 Some languages mark evidential meaning with a suffix.
sceneCN: 这里 evidential 指与证据来源有关的（第 1 个义项：与证据相关的、属于证据范畴的）；句意为有些语言用后缀标示示证意义。图中可辨识物件：白板、词尾卡片、箭头、声波图。

pos.zh: 证据的；可作证据的；证据性的
（语言学）示证的；标示信息来源的

senses.title: Relating to evidence
senses.definition: relating to evidence in general, especially in legal and scientific settings
senses.definitionCN: 与证据有关，多用于法律与研究语境
senses.example: The note has evidential value for the historian.
senses.exampleCN: 这份记录对史学家具有证据价值。
senses.why: Evidential is evidence plus the adjective suffix -al, so it names the whole class of things that have to do with proof.
senses.whyCN: evidential 是 evidence 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，因此指一切与证明有关的属性。

senses.title: Usable as evidence
senses.definition: able to be used as evidence in a case or an inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 可在案件或调查中作为证据使用
senses.example: Only the signed sheets were evidential; the drafts were not.
senses.exampleCN: 只有签过字的纸张才算证据，草稿不算。
senses.why: The suffix turns a broad relation into a qualification: a thing becomes evidential when a rule allows it into the record.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀把宽泛的关联变成一种资格：当规则允许某物进入案卷时，它就成其为证据性材料。

senses.title: Reasoning from proof
senses.definition: based on evidence rather than on assumption or authority
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据而非假设或权威进行的
senses.example: Evidential reasoning asks what the traces would look like if each hypothesis were true.
senses.exampleCN: 依据证据的推理会追问：若各个假设成立，痕迹会是什么样。
senses.why: Once proof items exist they can be weighed against competing accounts, and the adjective attaches to the method rather than the item.
senses.whyCN: 证据一旦存在，就能与不同说法相互衡量，这个形容词于是附着在方法上，而不是某件材料上。

senses.title: The linguistic category
senses.definition: marking how the speaker knows something, as through sight, hearsay or inference
senses.definitionCN: 标示说话者如何得知某事的语法范畴，如亲见、传闻或推断
senses.example: Some languages mark evidential meaning with a suffix.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言用后缀标示示证意义。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the adjective for grammar because a suffix can state the source of the speaker's evidence.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把这一形容词借到语法领域，因为一个后缀就能交代说话者证据的来源。

senses.title: The burden in litigation
senses.definition: the evidential burden: the duty to produce enough proof for a matter to be considered
senses.definitionCN: 在「举证负担」这一术语中，指为使某一争点进入审理而须提出足够证据的责任
senses.example: The evidential burden shifts once the defence raises the alibi.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提出不在场证明后，举证负担随之转移。
senses.why: Procedure separates the duty to persuade from the duty to bring proof, and this adjective marks the narrower one.
senses.whyCN: 程序法把「说服责任」与「提出证据的责任」分开，这个形容词标的是较窄的那一种。

senses.title: Weight in assessment
senses.definition: the strength that a piece of proof carries when findings are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较各项结论时某份材料所具有的证明力度
senses.example: The two studies carry different evidential weight.
senses.exampleCN: 这两项研究的证据分量不同。
senses.why: Once proof items are weighed rather than merely listed, the adjective moves from kind to degree.
senses.whyCN: 当证据不只是被列出、而是被衡量时，这个形容词就从「类别」转向「程度」。

senses.title: Indicative of something
senses.titleCN: 表明某种迹象的（旧用法）
senses.definition: serving as a sign of something, an older sense close to indicative
senses.definitionCN: 充当某事物的迹象，这一旧义接近 indicative
senses.example: A steady pulse was evidential of recovery in the old medical texts.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧医学文本里，平稳的脉搏是康复的迹象。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is visibility, so anything that makes a condition visible can still be called evidential.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的意思是「可见」，因此凡能让某种状况变得可见的东西仍可称为 evidential。

senses.title: Of physical proof in forensics
senses.titleCN: 法庭科学中的物证属性
senses.definition: relating to physical items handled as proof in forensic work
senses.definitionCN: 与法庭科学中作为证据处理的实物有关
senses.example: The evidential material was dried before it was packed.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据材料在封装前先被晾干。
senses.why: Forensic labs use the adjective for the physical half of a case, the objects that can be measured and sealed.
senses.whyCN: 法庭实验室用这个形容词指案件中的实物那一半，即可以测量与封存的东西。

intro.en: Evidential is formed inside English from evidence plus the adjective suffix -al, and is recorded from the nineteenth century. Evidence itself comes from Latin evidentia 'clearness', built on e- 'out' and videre 'to see'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: evidential 是在英语内部由 evidence 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，十九世纪起有记录。evidence 本身来自拉丁 evidentia「清楚」，由 e-「向外」与 videre「看见」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Evidentia named clearness or distinctness, from evidens 'visible, clear'.
items.cn: evidentia 指清楚、分明，出自 evidens「可见的、清楚的」。

items.en: English evidence first meant obviousness and later the material that makes a fact clear.
items.cn: 英语 evidence 最初指显而易见，后来指使事实变得清楚的材料。

items.en: -al, from Latin -alis, forms adjectives meaning 'relating to'; attached to evidence it yields evidential.
items.cn: -al 出自拉丁 -alis，构成表示「与……有关」的形容词；加在 evidence 上就得到 evidential。

items.en: The adjective spread in legal and philosophical writing, where proof and the testing of proof were being separated.
items.cn: 这个形容词在法律与哲学写作中流传开来，当时人们正把「证明」与「对证明的检验」区分开来。

items.en: In the twentieth century linguists applied it to grammatical markers of the source of knowledge, and the noun evidentiality followed.
items.cn: 二十世纪语言学家把它用于标示知识来源的语法标记，随后出现了名词 evidentiality。

items.en: The chain evidence plus -al is clear; only the exact year of the earliest citation is uncertain, so the adjective is dated to the nineteenth century as an approximation.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：evidence 加 -al 这条词源链清楚，只有最早书证的确切年份不确定，因此把形容词的首见年代按十九世纪作为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same family and one false friend; group two holds adjectives that also speak about proof but from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族成员与一个假朋友；第二组是同样谈论证明、但角度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: Means clear or obvious; it describes the fact, while evidential describes the proof of the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 意为明显、清楚；它描述事实本身，evidential 描述证明该事实的材料。

entries.definition: The adverb of evident, used for conclusions the speaker draws, not for rules about proof.
entries.definitionCN: evident 的副词，用于说话者自己得出的结论，而不是关于证据的规则。

entries.definition: From evincere, built on vincere 'to conquer': to display a quality, not to relate to evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 evincere，词根是 vincere「征服」：显出某种品质，与「证据」无关。

entries.definition: The grammatical category itself, formed from evidential plus -ity; the adjective names what the noun studies.
entries.definitionCN: 指示证这一语法范畴本身，由 evidential 加 -ity 构成；形容词指该范畴所修饰的东西。

entries.definition: From probare 'to test': having the power to prove something, a stronger claim than merely relating to proof.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 probare「检验」：具有证明力，比「与证据有关」更强。

entries.definition: Serving as a sign of something; it stops short of formal proof.
entries.definitionCN: 充当某事物的迹象，尚未达到正式证明。

entries.definition: Permitted by the rules of a court to be considered as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 依法院规则获准作为证据加以考虑。

entries.definition: From corroborare 'to strengthen': adding weight to proof that already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 corroborare「加强」：为已有证据增加分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Evidence plus -al: the adjective of proof.
normal.cn: evidence 加 -al：证据的形容词形式。

normal.en: The family runs evidence, evident, evidential, evidentiality, evidently.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evidence、evident、evidential、evidentiality 与 evidently。

normal.en: Legal usage pairs it with burden and value: evidential burden, evidential value.
normal.cn: 法律用法常与 burden、value 搭配：举证负担、证据价值。

normal.en: Linguistics pairs it with marker and system: evidential marker, evidential system.
normal.cn: 语言学常与 marker、system 搭配：示证标记、示证系统。

normal.en: Evince is a false friend from the conquering root.
normal.cn: evince 是假朋友，来自「征服」的词根。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a box stating where its contents came from.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子上贴着标签，写明里面的东西从哪来。

abstract.en: Picture a set of scales that weighs proofs instead of counting them.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，称的是证据的分量而不是件数。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence ending in a small tag that says how the speaker knows.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话末尾附着小标记，交代说话者是怎么知道的。

examples.en: The diary is evidential for the price of bread but not for the king's thoughts.
examples.cn: 这本日记对面包价格有证据价值，却不足以说明国王的想法。

examples.en: Her silence was evidential of nothing except exhaustion.
examples.cn: 她的沉默除了疲惫之外说明不了什么。

examples.en: The language marks hearsay with an evidential particle.
examples.cn: 这门语言用示证助词标示传闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evidence（证据）+ al（……的）」——关于证据的、能当证据的

root: 英语 evidence（证据）+ 形容词后缀 -al；evidence 出自拉丁 evidentia「清楚」= e-（向外）+ videre「看见」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses widen one relation: first a general tie to proof, then fitness for the record, then reasoning, a grammatical category, a procedural duty, a measured weight, an older sense of 'indicative' and the physical objects of a laboratory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把一个关系逐步撑开：先是与证据的一般关联，再是可入案的资格、依证据推理、语法范畴、程序义务、可衡量的分量、较旧的「表明」义，最后是实验室里的实物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered evidence bags laid out beside a whiteboard that traces where each item came from.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着编号的证据袋一字排开，旁边白板画出每件东西的来源路径。

branches.en: THE PROOF RELATION: the adjective ties an object to proof, then asks whether a rule lets it in.
branches.cn: 与证据的关系：先指某物与证据有关，再问规则是否允许它入案。

branches.en: REASONING: conclusions are drawn from traces rather than from authority.
branches.cn: 推理：结论取自痕迹，而不是取自权威。

branches.en: THE GRAMMATICAL MARK: a suffix states whether the speaker saw, heard or inferred the thing.
branches.cn: 语法标记：一个后缀说明说话者是亲见、听闻还是推断。

branches.en: DUTY AND WEIGHT: procedure assigns who must bring proof, and assessment asks how much it is worth.
branches.cn: 义务与分量：程序规定谁须举证，评估则问这份证据值多少。

branches.en: SIGN AND OBJECT: the older sense merely points at a sign, while forensics returns the word to sealed physical items.
branches.cn: 迹象与实物：较旧的义项只是指向迹象，法庭科学则把这个词带回封存的实物。

intro.en: Evidential is an English adjective built on evidence; both parts of the Latin source still build words in English.
intro.cn: evidential 是建立在 evidence 之上的英语形容词；其拉丁来源的两个部分在英语中仍在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives vision and video, and e- 'out' shapes evident, evidence and evidential.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 衍生 vision 与 video，而 e-「向外」塑造了 evident、evidence 与 evidential。

items.example: The prefix brings the fact into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把事实带到人眼前。
这个词根提供「看见」的意思。

items.example: The pattern was evident in the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个规律在数据中很明显。
这一主张在证据上很薄弱。

items.meaningCN: 示证性；信息来源的语法标示
items.example: Evidentiality is common in the language.
items.exampleCN: 示证性在这门语言中很常见。
这家诊所采用循证做法。

definition_zh: 化石；化石标本；化石燃料（作定语）；老顽固；过时的制度或观念
definition_en: the preserved remains or trace of an animal or plant from a past geological age, or something outdated
core_image: 页岩被劈开，一片鱼形的黑色印痕露出来，鳞片排列仍看得清
scene: 页岩劈开时，一片鱼形的黑色印痕露出来，鳞片排列还看得清。 The split shale revealed a fish fossil with scales still legible.
sceneCN: 这里 fossil 指「保存在岩层中的古生物遗体」（第 1 个义项：地质时期生物的保存遗体或印痕）；句意为劈开的页岩中露出一具鱼化石，鳞片仍清晰可辨。图中可辨识物件：劈开的页岩、鱼形印痕、鳞片纹理、地质锤。

pos.zh: 化石；化石标本；（口语）老顽固、过时的人或物
化石的；从化石中得来的（如 fossil fuel）

senses.title: Preserved remains in rock
senses.titleCN: 保存在岩层中的古生物遗体
senses.definition: the remains, impression or cast of an organism preserved in rock from an earlier geological period
senses.definitionCN: 保存在较早地质时期岩层中的生物遗体、印痕或铸型
senses.example: The museum's oldest fossil is a fern print from the Carboniferous.
senses.exampleCN: 馆藏最古老的化石是一件石炭纪的蕨类印痕。
senses.why: the Latin word meant 'dug up', so any organic trace hard enough to survive in stone qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词义为「挖出来的」，因此任何硬到能在石中留存的生物痕迹都算。

senses.title: A specimen in a collection
senses.definition: one catalogued piece held in a museum or study collection, with a number and a locality
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆或研究收藏中编了号、记了产地的一件标本
senses.example: Each fossil in the drawer carries a label with its grid reference.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里每件化石都带着写有网格坐标的标签。
senses.why: collecting practice turns the mass noun into a countable object, so a fossil can be borrowed, cast and photographed.
senses.whyCN: 收藏实践把不可数的总称变成可数物件，于是化石可以出借、翻模与拍摄。

senses.title: A species that has barely changed
senses.titleCN: 存活至今而形态几乎未变的物种
senses.definition: a living species that closely resembles its ancient relatives and has changed very little
senses.definitionCN: 与远古亲属极为相似、变化极小的现存物种
senses.example: The ginkgo is often called a living fossil, though its genes have moved on.
senses.exampleCN: 银杏常被称为活化石，尽管其基因已经变化。
senses.why: the phrase is a deliberate paradox: the organism is alive, yet read as if it were stone.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是刻意的悖论：生物还活着，却像石头一样被解读。

senses.title: Fuel from ancient organic matter
senses.titleCN: 源自远古有机质的燃料
senses.definition: coal, oil or gas formed from buried organisms and burned as fuel, used attributively
senses.definitionCN: 由埋藏的远古生物形成、被燃烧作燃料的煤、石油或天然气，作定语使用
senses.example: The city pledged to cut fossil fuel use by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 该市承诺把化石燃料用量削减三分之一。
senses.why: the attributive use compresses a long history: the fuel is ancient sunlight stored in rock.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法压缩了一段长历史：这种燃料是储在岩石里的远古阳光。

senses.title: A person stuck in the past
senses.titleCN: 口语：思想陈旧的老顽固
senses.definition: a person with fixed, old-fashioned views who resists any change
senses.definitionCN: 观念固定、守旧、抗拒任何改变的人
senses.example: The committee's chairman is an old fossil who still uses a typewriter.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会主席是个还在用打字机的老顽固。
senses.why: the insult works because a fossil is something that stopped changing long ago and now merely persists.
senses.whyCN: 这个贬称之所以有效，是因为化石早已停止变化，只是仍留在那里。

senses.title: An outdated institution or idea
senses.definition: a rule, practice or idea that survives long after its conditions have gone
senses.definitionCN: 在原有条件消失后仍存留很久的规则、做法或观念
senses.example: The licensing rule is a fossil of the cartage era.
senses.exampleCN: 这项许可规定是马车运输时代留下的化石。
senses.why: institutions leave traces the way organisms do, so the metaphor transfers without much strain.
senses.whyCN: 制度像生物一样留下痕迹，因此这个比喻转移过来并不费力。

senses.title: A trace fossil
senses.titleCN: 遗迹化石（活动留下的痕迹）
senses.definition: a preserved record of an organism's activity, such as a track, burrow or feeding mark, rather than its body
senses.definitionCN: 生物活动而非遗体留下的保存记录，如足迹、潜穴或觅食痕
senses.example: The sandstone holds trace fossils but no bones at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这层砂岩只有遗迹化石，完全没有骨骼。
senses.why: palaeontology separates the body from the behaviour, and the compound keeps that distinction visible.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学把遗体与行为分开，这个复合词让这一区分保持可见。

senses.title: A fossil used for dating
senses.definition: a species whose known time range lets a rock layer be assigned an age
senses.definitionCN: 已知生存时限可用于给岩层定年的物种
senses.example: A single ammonite fossil fixed the bed to the Jurassic.
senses.exampleCN: 一件菊石化石把这层定为侏罗纪。
senses.why: biostratigraphy treats certain fossils as index markers, valued for their date rather than their beauty.
senses.whyCN: 生物地层学把某些化石当作标志物，看重的是年代而非美观。

senses.title: Anything preserved in stone
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：被保存在石头里的
senses.definition: preserved in rock, or made of the mineral matter that replaced an organism
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石中的，或由替换生物体的矿物质构成的
senses.example: The fossil wood still shows annual growth rings.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石木仍能看到年轮。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the oldest literal sense, describing the state of preservation rather than a category of object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留最古老的字面义，描写保存状态，而非物类。

intro.en: Fossil comes from Latin fossilis 'dug up', from fodere 'to dig'. English adopted it in the seventeenth century for anything dug from the earth, before it narrowed to organic remains. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fossil 来自拉丁 fossilis「挖出来的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」。英语于十七世纪引入，最初泛指从地下挖出之物，后来收窄为生物遗体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fodere meant 'to dig', and its participle fossus produced fossilis 'dug up, dug out'.
items.cn: fodere 意为「挖掘」，其分词 fossus 产生 fossilis「被挖出的」。

items.en: In sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Latin, fossilis covered minerals, gems and anything else dug from the ground, not only living things.
items.cn: 在十六、十七世纪的拉丁语中，fossilis 涵盖矿物、宝石以及一切从地下挖出之物，并不限于生物。

items.en: English naturalists gradually restricted fossil to the remains and traces of once-living things found in rock.
items.cn: 英国博物学者逐渐把 fossil 收窄为岩石中发现的、曾属生物的那些遗体与痕迹。

items.en: The nineteenth century added fossil fuel, and the same period produced the joking use for an out-of-date person.
items.cn: 十九世纪增添了 fossil fuel 一义，同一时期也产生了戏指过时之人的用法。

items.en: The phrase living fossil was applied to species that seem unchanged since deep time, an image rather than a taxonomic category.
items.cn: living fossil 一语用于自远古以来似无变化的物种，是意象而非分类学范畴。

items.en: Source uncertain (only the first dating is in doubt): the Latin derivation is secure, but the exact decade of the English narrowing varies by author.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁派生是确定的，但英语收窄的确切年代因作者而异。

note.en: Group one separates fossil from words built on the same Latin dig-family and from look-alikes; group two separates it from other remains and from the figurative senses.
note.cn: 第一组把 fossil 与同出拉丁「挖」族的词及形近词分开；第二组区分它与其它遗体说法及比喻义。

entries.definition: To make or become a fossil; the noun names the object, the verb the process.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为化石或变成化石；名词指对象，动词指过程。

entries.definition: Fossil plus -ferous 'bearing': rock that contains fossils, said of a layer.
entries.definitionCN: fossil 加 -ferous「承载」：含化石的，用于形容岩层。

entries.definition: From Latin fossa 'a ditch', also from fodere; it means a trench, not a remain.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fossa「沟」，亦出 fodere；意为壕沟，而非遗体。

entries.definition: An Australian English verb for prospecting among old workings; its origin is uncertain and not the Latin fossilis line.
entries.definitionCN: 澳大利亚英语动词，指在旧矿渣中搜寻；来源不确定，不属拉丁 fossilis 一线。

entries.definition: Something that survives from an earlier time, including objects and customs; it need not be mineralised.
entries.definitionCN: 从较早时期留存之物，包括器物与习俗；不必矿化。

entries.definition: What is left of a body, recent or ancient; fossil adds deep time and preservation in rock.
entries.definitionCN: 遗体残留，不论新旧；fossil 增添深时间与岩中保存之意。

entries.definition: A replica formed when minerals fill a mould left by a dissolved organism; one kind of fossil.
entries.definitionCN: 矿物填充生物溶解后留下的模腔所形成的复制体，是化石的一种。

entries.definition: A body preserved by drying or cold rather than mineralisation; it is not usually called a fossil.
entries.definitionCN: 靠干燥或寒冷而非矿化保存的尸体，通常不称化石。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin fossilis 'dug up' from fodere 'to dig': what the hammer brings out of the rock.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fossilis「挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖」：锤子从岩中取出的东西。

normal.en: The family runs fossil, fossils, fossilize, fossilization, fossiliferous, subfossil.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fossil、fossils、fossilize、fossilization、fossiliferous、subfossil。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fossil record, fossil fuel, trace fossil, living fossil.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：化石记录、化石燃料、遗迹化石、活化石。

normal.en: The same Latin dig-root gives fosse 'ditch', a hole rather than a remain.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁「挖」根还给出 fosse「壕沟」，是洞而非遗体。

normal.en: The insult is geological: something that stopped changing long ago and merely persists.
normal.cn: 这个贬称是地质式的：早已停止变化，只是仍留在那里。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf pressed into mud and read a million years later.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子压进泥里，百万年后被读出。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that stopped at noon and was never wound again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只停在正午、再没上过发条的钟。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook still in force for a machine nobody owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一本仍有效的规程，而其机器已无人拥有。

examples.en: The fossil was prepared with needles over three months.
examples.cn: 这件化石用针修整了三个月。

examples.en: Burning fossil fuel returns stored carbon to the air.
examples.cn: 燃烧化石燃料把储藏的碳送回大气。

examples.en: His views on office work are frankly fossil.
examples.cn: 他对办公室工作的看法坦白说过时了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「foss（挖）+ il」——从地下挖出来的东西 → 化石、老古董

root: 拉丁 fossilis「挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」；英语十七世纪借入，原泛指地下挖出之物，后收窄为生物遗体。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with something dug from rock, then split into specimen, living paradox, fuel, insult, institution, trace, dating tool and adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「从岩中挖出之物」开始，随后分出标本、活着的悖论、燃料、贬称、制度、遗迹、定年工具与形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape in stone that once was alive and will not change again.
core.cn: 核心意象：石中一个曾经活着的形状，再也不会改变。

branches.en: PRESERVED FORM: the noun and the adjective describe the same mineral state.
branches.cn: 保存的形态：名词与形容词描写同一种矿物状态。

branches.en: OBJECT AND TOOL: one fossil is a specimen, another is a date.
branches.cn: 对象与工具：一件是标本，另一件是年代。

branches.en: TRACES OF LIFE: a living species and a burrow both count as traces of the ancient.
branches.cn: 生命的痕迹：现存物种与潜穴都算远古痕迹。

branches.en: STORED SUNLIGHT: fuel is the same burial read as energy.
branches.cn: 储存的阳光：燃料是同一种埋藏被读作能量。

branches.en: FROZEN THINGS: a person and a rule both stopped changing and merely persist.
branches.cn: 冻住之物：人与规则都停止变化，只是仍留在那里。

intro.en: Fossil is a Latin adjective turned noun, and its root recurs in English words about digging and ditches.
intro.cn: fossil 是拉丁形容词转成的名词，其词根在英语中反复出现于与挖掘、沟渠有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fodere 'to dig' gives fossilis 'dug up', fossa 'ditch' and fossor 'digger'; English adds -ize, -ization and -ferous to extend the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fodere「挖」产生 fossilis「挖出的」、fossa「沟」与 fossor「挖掘者」；英语用 -ize、-ization、-ferous 扩展词族。

items.structure: fodere / fossus (Latin verb and participle 'dig, dug')
items.example: The root names the act of digging out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名挖出的动作。

items.example: The fossil came out in three pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这块化石裂成三块取出。
矿物水能使骨骼化石化。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fossil

items.example: A fossiliferous limestone forms the ledge.
items.exampleCN: 一层含化石的石灰岩构成这级岩台。

items.example: Subfossil bones come from recent caves.
items.exampleCN: 亚化石骨骼出自较近的洞穴。

items.example: The fosse lies outside the wall.
They fossick for opals on the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 他们在山脊翻找蛋白石。

definition_zh: adj./adv. 顺时针方向的（地）
definition_en: moving in the direction in which the hands of a clock turn
core_image: 钟表的指针一圈圈向右转
scene: 他把瓶盖按顺时针方向拧紧。 He turned the lid clockwise to tighten it.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clockwise 指顺时针方向；句意是他把瓶盖按顺时针方向拧紧。

senses.title: In the direction of clock hands
senses.definition: moving the way the hands of a clock move, left to right over the top
senses.definitionCN: 像指针那样越过顶端从左向右移动
senses.example: Turn the key clockwise to open the door.
senses.exampleCN: 顺时针拧钥匙开门。
senses.why: Clock and wise join to name the direction of hands.
senses.whyCN: clock 与 wise 组合，指指针行进的方向。

senses.title: Arranged in that order
senses.definition: placed or ordered in the same circular direction
senses.definitionCN: 按同一环形方向排列或排序
senses.example: The dancers moved clockwise around the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者沿着大厅顺时针移动。
senses.why: The direction word also describes order.
senses.whyCN: 这个方向词也用来描述次序。

intro.en: Clockwise was coined in the nineteenth century from clock plus an old suffix of manner.
intro.cn: clockwise 是十九世纪用 clock 加古代表方式的词缀构成。

items.en: Clock comes from Dutch klok, a bell.
items.cn: clock 来自荷兰语 klok（钟）。

items.en: Wise once meant manner or way, as in likewise.
items.cn: wise 古义为方式，如 likewise。

items.en: Clockwise appears as clock faces spread.
items.cn: 1870 年代随钟面普及而出现。

items.en: Engineers use it for screws and dials.
items.cn: 二十世纪工程师用它描述螺丝与旋钮。

items.en: Anticlockwise serves as its opposite.
items.cn: 现代 anticlockwise 作其反义词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -wise ending; the near-meaning group names turning and direction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -wise 结尾；近义组列出转动与方向的说法。

entries.definition: A spring-driven mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 发条机构。

entries.definition: In the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 同样地。

entries.definition: In another way.
entries.definitionCN: 否则；另外。

entries.definition: Turning against clock hands.
entries.definitionCN: 逆时针的。

entries.definition: In the direction of the sun.
entries.definitionCN: 顺日行方向。

entries.definition: Moving in a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 旋转地。

normalIntro.en: Follow the clock hands: that way is clockwise.
normalIntro.cn: 跟着钟表指针走：那个方向就是顺时针。

normal.en: Clock hands go clockwise.
normal.cn: 钟表指针走的就是顺时针。

normal.en: Wise here means way.
normal.cn: 这里的 wise 意为方式。

normal.en: Turn a lid clockwise to close it.
normal.cn: 顺时针拧盖子是关上。

normal.en: The opposite is anticlockwise.
normal.cn: 反义词是 anticlockwise。

normal.en: Screws usually tighten clockwise.
normal.cn: 螺丝通常顺时针拧紧。

abstract.en: Hands chasing their own tail.
abstract.cn: 指针追着自己的尾巴。

abstract.en: A direction borrowed from a face.
abstract.cn: 从钟面借来的方向。

abstract.en: Time drawn as an arrow.
abstract.cn: 被画成箭头的时光。

examples.en: Rotate the dial clockwise until it clicks.
examples.cn: 把旋钮顺时针转到咔的一声。

examples.en: The seats are numbered clockwise from the door.
examples.cn: 座位从门口起顺时针编号。

examples.en: Swirl the glass clockwise and smell the wine.
examples.cn: 顺时针晃杯，闻一闻酒香。

dict_mnemonic.text: clock（钟）+ wise（方式）→ 按钟表指针的方式，即顺时针。

root: 荷兰 klok（钟）→ 英语 clock + 古英语 wise（方式）→ 十九世纪 clock-wise

sensesIntro.en: A clock face taught the language a word for direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 钟面教会了语言一个方向词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin hands sweeping over the top of a dial
core.cn: 核心意象：细指针扫过表盘顶部

branches.en: A key turning to the right.
branches.cn: 向右转动的钥匙。

branches.en: A lid screwed down tight.
branches.cn: 拧紧的瓶盖。

branches.en: Seats numbered round a hall.
branches.cn: 沿大厅编号的座位。

branches.en: Dancers moving in one order.
branches.cn: 按同一顺序移动的舞者。

branches.en: A direction that also orders space.
branches.cn: 既是方向，也是排序。

intro.en: Clockwise joins a clock to an old manner suffix; the list adds turning words.
intro.cn: clockwise 由 clock 与古代表方式的词缀组成；下面列出转动词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rota is a wheel, vertere is to turn, and contra is against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rota 意为轮，vertere 意为转，contra 意为相反。

latinEntries.exampleCN: rota 产生 rotate 与 rotation。
vertere 产生 reverse 与 version。
contra 产生 contradict 与 contrary。

definition_zh: 向后靠；斜倚；使（座椅）后仰；躺靠
definition_en: to lean the body or a seat backwards into a resting position
core_image: 椅背一格一格向后倒，人的重心慢慢交给它
scene: 他把椅背调到最低，几乎躺着看完了那场电影。 He reclined the seat as far as it would go and watched the film almost lying down.
sceneCN: 这里 recline 指把座椅向后调（第 1 个义项：使座椅后仰）；句意为他把椅背调到最低，几乎躺着看完了那场电影。

pos.zh: 向后靠；斜倚；使（座椅）后仰

senses.title: To recline the seat
senses.definition: to tilt a seat backwards so the body can rest
senses.definitionCN: 把座椅向后倾斜，让身体可以休息
senses.example: He reclined the seat as far as it would go.
senses.exampleCN: 他把椅背调到最低。
senses.why: The first sense is mechanical: a hinge does the work.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是机械的：干活的是铰链。

senses.title: To recline on a sofa
senses.definition: to lie back on a soft surface at an angle
senses.definitionCN: 以一个角度仰卧在柔软的表面上
senses.example: She reclined on the sofa with a book over her face.
senses.exampleCN: 她斜倚在沙发上，书盖在脸上。
senses.why: Here the body, not a mechanism, is the subject.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是身体，而不是机械。

senses.title: To recline against a wall
senses.definition: to lean the back against a support and let it carry part of the weight
senses.definitionCN: 把背靠在支撑物上，让它承担一部分重量
senses.example: The guard reclined against the wall and watched the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵靠着墙，盯着大门。
senses.why: The sense is about borrowed support.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是借来的支撑。

senses.title: A reclining chair
senses.definition: furniture built so the back can be lowered
senses.definitionCN: 靠背可以被放低的家具
senses.example: A reclining chair took up half the room.
senses.exampleCN: 一把躺椅占了半间屋子。
senses.why: The participle becomes a permanent product label.
senses.whyCN: 分词变成一个固定的商品标签。

senses.title: To recline at an angle
senses.definition: to set the body or a seat at a measured slope
senses.definitionCN: 把身体或座椅调到一个有度数的斜度
senses.example: The dentist reclined the chair to thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医把椅子调到三十度。
senses.why: The sense brings the word close to measurement.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项让这个词靠近测量。

senses.title: To recline in the shade
senses.definition: to rest outdoors in a leaning posture
senses.definitionCN: 在户外以一种斜靠的姿势休息
senses.example: They reclined in the shade and let the afternoon pass.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在荫处躺靠着，让午后过去。
senses.why: The word carries leisure, not just posture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着闲暇，不只是姿势。

senses.title: Reclining as ease
senses.definition: the posture that signals trust and unhurried time
senses.definitionCN: 一种表示信任与不慌不忙的姿态
senses.example: His reclining manner annoyed the examiner.
senses.exampleCN: 他那副靠着的闲散样子让考官不快。
senses.why: Posture is read as an attitude by others.
senses.whyCN: 姿势会被别人读成一种态度。

senses.title: Versus lie
senses.definition: to lean back into a support, as opposed to being flat
senses.definitionCN: 向后倚入支撑，与平躺相对
senses.example: You recline in a chair; you lie on a floor.
senses.exampleCN: 你在椅子里后靠，你在地板上平躺。
senses.why: The pair separates angle from horizontality.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把角度与水平分开。

intro.en: Recline comes from Latin reclinare, 'to lean back', from re-, 'back', and clinare, 'to bend'.
intro.cn: recline 来自拉丁语 reclinare（向后倾），由 re-（向后）与 clinare（弯曲）构成。

items.en: Clinare meant to bend or slant.
items.cn: clinare 意为弯曲或倾斜。

items.en: The compound meant to bend something backwards.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为把某物向后弯。

items.en: English first used the word of bodies and couches.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指身体与卧榻。

items.en: Railway and garden chairs made reclining a product.
items.cn: 火车与花园椅让 reclining 成为商品。

items.en: Today it covers seats, patients and leisure.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖座椅、病人与闲暇。

note.en: The look-alike group is the clin- family; the near-meaning group separates lean, lounge, slouch and sprawl.
note.cn: 形近组是 clin 词族；近义组把「倚」「闲躺」「瘫坐」「摊开四肢」分开。

entries.definition: to refuse or to decrease.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝或下降。

entries.definition: to lean forward or to tend.
entries.definitionCN: 前倾或倾向。

entries.definition: a chair that reclines.
entries.definitionCN: 可后仰的椅子。

entries.definition: leaning backwards.
entries.definitionCN: 向后靠的。

entries.definition: to rest against something at an angle.
entries.definitionCN: 以某个角度倚靠某物。

entries.definition: to rest in a relaxed way.
entries.definitionCN: 以放松的方式休息。

entries.definition: to sit or stand with a drooping posture.
entries.definitionCN: 以塌下的姿势坐或站。

entries.definition: to spread the limbs out loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 手脚松垮地摊开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a seat back falling one notch at a time.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「椅背一格一格向后倒」的画面。

normal.en: Recline contains clin, Latin for bending: the back bends.
normal.cn: recline 里有 clin（拉丁语的弯）：背弯下去。

normal.en: Picture a hinge giving way and the body's weight moving back.
normal.cn: 想象铰链松开，身体的重量向后移。

normal.en: Say rih-KLINE; it rhymes with the line of a slanted chair.
normal.cn: 读 rih-KLINE，与斜椅那条线押韵。

normal.en: The word needs a support: a seat, a sofa, a wall.
normal.cn: 这个词需要一个支撑：座椅、沙发、墙。

normal.en: Ask how far back, and who is holding the weight.
normal.cn: 问后仰到多远，谁在承担重量。

abstract.en: Reclining is a small surrender of balance to furniture.
abstract.cn: 后靠是把平衡稍稍交给家具。

abstract.en: The angle of a body is a social statement before it is a comfort.
abstract.cn: 身体的倾斜角度先是一项社会表态，然后才是舒适。

abstract.en: What holds you up also sets how far you may lean.
abstract.cn: 支撑你的东西，也决定你能靠多远。

examples.en: She reclined on the sofa with a book over her face.
examples.cn: 她斜倚在沙发上，书盖在脸上。

examples.en: The guard reclined against the wall and watched the gate.
examples.cn: 卫兵靠着墙，盯着大门。

examples.en: They reclined in the shade and let the afternoon pass.
examples.cn: 他们在荫处躺靠着，让午后过去。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（向后）+ cline（弯）→ 把身子往后弯。

root: 拉丁语 reclinare（向后倾）← re-（向后）+ clinare（弯曲）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses lean one body back: a seat, a sofa, a wall, a chair as product, a measured angle, outdoor shade, a manner read by others, and the line to lying flat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把同一个身体往后靠：座椅、沙发、墙、作为商品的椅子、量过的角度、户外的荫、被别人读出的姿态，以及与平躺的界线。

core.en: A SEAT BACK FALLING BY NOTCHES
core.cn: 一格一格倒下的椅背

branches.en: A seat adjusted and furniture designed for it.
branches.cn: 被调节的座椅与为此设计的家具。

branches.en: Soft surfaces indoors and shade outdoors.
branches.cn: 室内的软面与户外的荫。

branches.en: A wall that carries part of the weight.
branches.cn: 承担部分重量的墙。

branches.en: A measured slope and a manner others interpret.
branches.cn: 量出的斜度与别人解读的姿态。

branches.en: Leaning against flat lying.
branches.cn: 倚靠与平躺相对。

intro.en: The clin- family is about slanting: recline bends back, incline bends forward, decline bends away or downward.
intro.cn: clin 词族讲的是倾斜：recline 向后弯，incline 向前弯，decline 弯开或向下。

latinIntro.en: Latin clinare gives the bend; the prefixes re-, in- and de- set the direction of every member of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clinare 给出弯曲；re-、in-、de- 这些前缀为词族的每个成员定下方向。

items.meaning: bedside practice, from the same bend

definition_zh: 人格特质；性格特征；可测量而相对稳定的行为倾向
definition_en: a stable, measurable tendency in a person's behaviour that forms part of the wider pattern of character
core_image: 一张织物的放大图：整块布看不出花样，退后一步才看见经线与纬线交织成的那道纹
scene: 同一份问卷发给上千人，答案里反复出现的那几条，最后被研究者画成了一条曲线。 One personality trait stood out across every age group in the survey.
sceneCN: 这里 personality trait 指「人格中一条可测量、相对稳定的倾向」（第 1 个义项：人格的可测倾向）；句意是有一项人格特质在所有年龄组里都很突出。图中可辨识物件：问卷、堆叠的答题纸、一条上升的曲线。

senses.title: One measurable tendency
senses.definition: a single stable tendency that can be rated and compared across people
senses.definitionCN: 一条稳定倾向，可被评级并在人与人之间比较
senses.example: One personality trait stood out across every age group.
senses.exampleCN: 有一项人格特质在所有年龄组里都很突出。
senses.why: the phrase narrows a whole pattern to one thread, which is what makes counting possible at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组把整块格局收窄成一根线，正是这一点让计数成为可能。

senses.title: A building block of character
senses.definition: a component out of which the larger pattern of a person is assembled
senses.definitionCN: 用来组装一个人更大格局的构件
senses.example: Patience is a personality trait that can be trained.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是一项可以训练的人格特质。
senses.why: a pattern needs parts, and this phrase names the parts rather than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 格局需要零件，这个词组命名的正是零件，而不是整体。

senses.title: A tendency that runs in families
senses.definition: a trait shown by studies to be partly inherited rather than wholly learned
senses.definitionCN: 研究显示部分来自遗传、而非完全习得的特质
senses.example: Shyness is treated as an inherited personality trait in some studies.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些研究里，害羞被当作一种可遗传的人格特质。
senses.why: once a trait is measured, the next question is where it comes from, and inheritance is one answer.
senses.whyCN: 特质一旦能被测量，下一个问题就是它从哪里来，遗传承是其中一个答案。

senses.title: One of the five dimensions
senses.definition: a member of the widely used five-factor classification of character
senses.definitionCN: 广为使用的五因素人格分类中的某一项
senses.example: Conscientiousness is the personality trait most tied to school results.
senses.exampleCN: 尽责性是五项人格特质中与学业成绩关系最紧的一项。
senses.why: classification reduces many traits to a few dims, and each of those dims is still called a trait.
senses.whyCN: 分类把许多特质压缩成少数几个维度，而其中每个维度仍被称为一项特质。

senses.title: A reading of how someone acts
senses.titleCN: 对某人行为方式的解读
senses.definition: the label an observer applies when the same behaviour keeps recurring
senses.definitionCN: 观察者在同一行为反复出现时贴上的标签
senses.example: Neatness is a personality trait only if it shows up without being asked.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当整洁无需要求便出现时，它才算一项人格特质。
senses.why: a trait is inferred from repetition, so it is a reading of behaviour rather than the behaviour itself.
senses.whyCN: 特质是从重复中推断出来的，因此它是对行为的解读，而不是行为本身。

senses.title: An item on an assessment form
senses.definition: a scored item in hiring, clinical or educational assessment
senses.definitionCN: 招聘、临床或教育测评中被打分的一栏
senses.example: The form lists twelve personality traits and asks for evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 表格列出十二项人格特质，并要求给出依据。
senses.why: institutions need comparable entries, so the phrase becomes a row on a form with a number beside it.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要可比较的条目，于是这个词组变成表格上的一行，旁边配一个数字。

senses.title: A trait that can be praised or blamed
senses.definition: the same tendency seen as a virtue in one setting and a fault in another
senses.definitionCN: 同一条倾向在一种场合被看作长处，在另一种场合被看作毛病
senses.example: Stubbornness is the same personality trait as persistence, seen from the other side.
senses.exampleCN: 固执与坚持是同一项人格特质，只是从另一面看。
senses.why: value is added by the observer, not by the trait, which is why the same behaviour gets two names.
senses.whyCN: 价值是观察者添上的，不是特质自带的，因此同一行为会有两个名字。

senses.title: A mark that identifies a character
senses.definition: in fiction and drama, a repeated habit used to make a figure recognisable
senses.definitionCN: 在小说与戏剧中，用来让人物可被辨认的重复习惯
senses.example: The writer gives each sister one personality trait and never adds a second.
senses.exampleCN: 作者只给每位姐妹一项人格特质，从不加第二项。
senses.why: storytelling borrows the research unit because one clear trait is enough to make a figure stick.
senses.whyCN: 叙事借用了研究的单位，因为一项清晰的特质就足以让人物留得住。

intro.en: The phrase joins personality, from Latin persona 'mask', with trait, from French and Latin tractus 'a drawing, a line'. It is a modern technical label of psychology and dates as a fixed phrase to the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词组把出自拉丁 persona「面具」的 personality，与出自法语及拉丁 tractus「划线、拉出」的 trait 接在一起。它是心理学的近代专业标签，作为固定说法大致定形于 20 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Persona meant a mask worn on stage and then the role itself; its deeper origin is uncertain, and one hypothesis links it to an Etruscan word.
items.cn: persona 指舞台上戴的面具，后指角色本身；其更深来源不确定，有一种假说认为它来自某种伊特鲁里亚词。

items.en: Tractus meant 'a drawing, a line, a pull', from trahere 'to draw'. French turned it into a word for a line or feature of the face or character.
items.cn: tractus 意为「划线、拉、牵引」，出自 trahere「拉」。法语把它变成指面部或性格的一条线、一个特征。

items.en: English borrowed trait in the sixteenth century for a stroke of the pen and then for a feature of body or mind.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 trait，先指一笔，后指身体或心智上的一个特征。

items.en: Nineteenth-century psychology needed countable units of character, and the phrase settled the noun trait into that role.
items.cn: 19 世纪心理学需要可计数的性格单位，这个词组把 trait 固定在这个角色上。

items.en: Twentieth-century factor analysis reduced many traits to five broad dimensions, and the phrase became standard in reports and tests.
items.cn: 20 世纪的因素分析把许多特质压缩成五个宽维度，这个词组遂成为报告与测验里的标准说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date at which the two words began to be used as a fixed phrase is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这两个词开始作为固定说法使用，确切年代没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that look similar and are often swapped; group two holds the neighbouring terms of trait research.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相近、常被互换的词组；第二组是特质研究里的邻近术语。

entries.definition: Nearly the same unit, but it leans toward moral qualities such as honesty, while this phrase leans toward measurable tendencies.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎同一个单位，但它偏向诚实一类道德品质，而本词组偏向可测量的倾向。

entries.definition: Names a category a person belongs to, not a single tendency, so the two answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 命名一个人所属的类别，而不是一条倾向，因此两者回答不同的问题。

entries.definition: A looser phrase that can cover habits and tastes; the technical form is this one.
entries.definitionCN: 较松的说法，可涵盖习惯与口味；专业形式是本词组。

entries.definition: The bare noun can belong to a species, a face or a character; adding personality restricts it to the human pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的名词可指物种、面容或人物的特征；加上 personality 就把范围限定为人的格局。

entries.definition: The native part of the pattern; traits may be inherited but are still measured one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 格局中天生的那部分；特质可以遗传，但仍是一条条被测量。

entries.definition: A repeated behaviour that may be learned; a trait is the disposition said to lie behind such repetitions.
entries.definitionCN: 可习得的重复行为；特质是被认为藏在这些重复背后的倾向。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a feature of a person or thing, with no claim about stability or measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或物某一特征的日常词，不主张稳定性或可测量性。

entries.definition: A feature assigned to someone, often by an observer; it carries less weight than a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 由他人赋予某人的特征，常出自观察者；分量不如 trait。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: First word from Latin for a mask, second word from Latin for a drawn line: a line on the mask.
normal.cn: 第一个词出自拉丁的「面具」，第二个词出自拉丁的「划出的线」：面具上的一道线。

normal.en: The family runs trait, personality, personality trait, character trait, trait theory.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 trait、personality、personality trait、character trait、trait theory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: the Big Five personality traits, measure personality traits, inherited personality trait.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：大五人格特质、测量人格特质、遗传的人格特质。

normal.en: Research distinguishes a trait from a type: one is a thread, the other is a box.
normal.cn: 研究区分「特质」与「类型」：一个是线，一个是盒子。

normal.en: The phrase is countable, which is why reports speak of twelve traits rather than one character.
normal.cn: 这个词组可数，因此报告会说十二项特质，而不是一个性格。

abstract.en: Picture a magnified cloth where a single thread can be pulled out and named.
abstract.cn: 想象一块放大的织物，能抽出一根线并为它命名。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dots on a chart that only becomes a line when enough people answer.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一排点，只有足够多人作答之后才连成一条线。

abstract.en: Picture the same key opening one door and jamming another.
abstract.cn: 想象同一把钥匙开了一扇门，却卡住了另一扇。

examples.en: Curiosity is the personality trait that predicts the widest range of outcomes.
examples.cn: 好奇心是能预测最多种结果的一项人格特质。

examples.en: The study compares personality traits across three generations.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了三代之间的人格特质。

examples.en: Punctuality is less a personality trait than a local custom.
examples.cn: 守时比起人格特质，更像是当地的风俗。

dict_mnemonic.text: personality（人格）+ trait（特征）——人格上的那一条特征 → 人格特质

root: 由 personality（拉丁 persona「面具」+ 抽象名词后缀）与 trait（拉丁 tractus「划线、拉出」）合成；作为固定说法属近代心理学专业标签。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a single thread is pulled out of a whole pattern, and that thread is then read as a component, as an inheritance, as a dimension, as a label, as a form entry, as a value judgement and finally as a storytelling mark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：从整块格局中抽出一根线，这根线依次被读作构件、遗传、维度、标签、表格栏目、价值判断，最后是叙事标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnified cloth where the whole weave is invisible until one thread is pulled out and named.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块放大的织物，整片织法看不见，直到抽出一根线并为它命名。

branches.en: THE THREAD AND THE WEAVE: the measured tendency first, then its job as a part of the larger pattern.
branches.cn: 线与织法：先是可测量的倾向，再是它作为更大格局之零件的作用。

branches.en: WHERE THE THREAD COMES FROM: inheritance is the research answer to why the same line keeps appearing.
branches.cn: 线从哪里来：遗传是研究给出的答案，解释了同一条线为何反复出现。

branches.en: THE THREAD AS A DIMENSION: factor analysis folds many threads into five broad bands.
branches.cn: 线作为维度：因素分析把许多线折成五条宽带。

branches.en: THE THREAD READ AND RECORDED: an observer's label, then a scored row on an assessment form.
branches.cn: 线被解读与被记录：先是观察者的标签，再是测评表上被打分的一行。

branches.en: ONE THREAD, TWO JUDGEMENTS: praised as persistence or blamed as stubbornness, and used by writers to make a figure stick.
branches.cn: 同一根线，两种判断：被赞为坚持或被责为固执，也被作家用来让人物留得住。

intro.en: Two Latin-derived words joined into a technical phrase; each half still reads by its own pieces.
intro.cn: 两个来自拉丁的词拼成一个专业词组，每一半仍可按自己的成分拆读。

latinIntro.en: Latin persona 'mask' supplies the first half through its abstract noun; Latin tractus 'a drawing' supplies the second through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 persona「面具」经其抽象名词提供前半；拉丁 tractus「划线」经法语提供后半。

items.example: The first half goes back to the stage mask.
items.exampleCN: 前半上溯到舞台上的面具。

items.example: It makes the first half abstract.
items.exampleCN: 它让前半变成抽象名词。

items.meaning: the whole pattern of a person
items.meaningCN: 一个人整体的性格格局

items.meaning: a drawing, a line, a pull

Neatness is one trait among many.

items.exampleCN: 有一项人格特质很突出。

items.meaningCN: 品性构成中的一项特征

items.meaning: the approach that explains people by stable traits
items.meaningCN: 用稳定特质解释人的理论取向
items.exampleCN: 特质理论是多数问卷的基础。

latinEntries.meaning: the quality of being a person

definition_zh: 低音；低音部；低音提琴；鲈鱼
definition_en: the lowest range of sound or voice; the low-frequency part of music; a food fish
core_image: 音响里让你胸口发麻的那层嗡鸣
scene: 调音师蹲在音箱后拧低频旋钮，地板随之轻颤。 Turn down the bass before the neighbors complain.
sceneCN: 这里 bass 指「低音」（第 1 个义项：音乐低频部分）；句意：在邻居投诉前把低音关小。

forms.label: 名词原形（低音义与鲈鱼义同形）

senses.title: The low part of music
senses.definition: the lowest range of pitches in music
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中最低的音区
senses.example: The organ's bass shook the cathedral floor.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴的低音震得教堂地板发颤。
senses.why: Latin bassus meant low; music took the word for the floor of sound.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bassus 意为「低」；音乐取之指声音的地板。

senses.title: The lowest male voice
senses.definition: the deepest singing voice of a man
senses.definitionCN: 男声中最低沉的声部
senses.example: He sings bass in the choir.
senses.exampleCN: 他在唱诗班唱男低音。
senses.why: The lowest part of the vocal range keeps the word.
senses.whyCN: 人声音域之最低者沿用此词。

senses.title: Low-frequency instruments
senses.definition: instruments designed for low pitch, as the double bass
senses.definitionCN: 为低音而设的乐器，如低音提琴
senses.example: A double bass stood behind the cellist.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴手身后立着一架低音提琴。
senses.why: Each instrument family places its low member here.
senses.whyCN: 各乐器家族的低音成员皆归此列。

senses.title: The fish
senses.definition: a food fish of fresh or sea water
senses.definitionCN: 淡水或海产的食用鱼
senses.example: They caught bass off the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在礁石外钓到鲈鱼。
senses.why: A different line: Old English bærs, perch, shortened to bass.
senses.whyCN: 另一词线：古英语 bærs「河鲈」缩略为 bass。

senses.title: Bass as amplifier power
senses.definition: strong low-frequency sound from speakers
senses.definitionCN: 音箱输出的强劲低频
senses.example: The car's bass rattled the windows.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车音响的低音震得车窗作响。
senses.why: Reproduction technology borrowed the musical word.
senses.whyCN: 放音技术借用音乐之词。

senses.title: Bass clef
senses.definition: the F clef used for low-pitched notation
senses.definitionCN: 标记低音的 F 谱号
senses.example: Left-hand piano parts are written in bass clef.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴左手声部记于低音谱号。
senses.why: Notation needs a flag for the basement of music.
senses.whyCN: 乐谱需要一面标记「地下室」的旗。

senses.title: Bass in mixed ensembles
senses.definition: the foundational layer supporting harmony
senses.definitionCN: 支撑和声的基础层
senses.example: A good bass line holds the whole band together.
senses.exampleCN: 好的贝斯线能把整支乐队拢住。
senses.why: The bottom carries the building again.
senses.whyCN: 底层再度承托整座建筑。

senses.title: Bass guitar
senses.definition: the four-string electric instrument of popular music
senses.definitionCN: 流行乐中四弦电声低音乐器
senses.example: She switched from guitar to bass.
senses.exampleCN: 她从吉他转弹贝斯。
senses.why: Electric times gave the bass its own instrument.
senses.whyCN: 电声时代让低音有了专属乐器。

intro.en: Bass is a respelling of base, from Latin bassus, low; the fish bass is a separate word from Old English bærs, perch.
intro.cn: bass 是 base 的改拼，出拉丁 bassus「低」；鲈鱼义之 bass 是另一词，出古英语 bærs「河鲈」。

items.en: The root behind bassus meant short, low.
items.cn: bassus 背后词根意为短、低。

items.en: bassus meant low of stature or pitch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bassus 指身矮或音低。

items.en: Italian basso carried the low voice into music.
items.cn: 意大利语 basso 把低音带入音乐。

items.en: English spelled the music word base, then adopted bass to tell it from base, foundation.
items.cn: 英语先拼作 base，后改拼 bass 以区别「基础」之 base。

items.en: The fish came from bærs, the perch, its b-r dropping out.
items.cn: 鲈鱼出 bærs「河鲈」，首音 b-r 脱落。

note.en: Group one holds the low family and look-alikes; group two holds the music-range field.
note.cn: 第一组收「低」词族与形近词；第二组收「音域」义场。

entries.definition: foundation or morally low; the spelling twin.
entries.definitionCN: 基础或卑鄙；拼写孪生词。

entries.definition: an Italian bass voice.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语男低音。

entries.definition: the person in charge of workers or an organization
entries.definitionCN: 老板；上司——只是与 bass 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the highest range of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 最高音区；反义对照。

entries.definition: the male voice just above bass.
entries.definitionCN: 男中音；高于男低音。

entries.definition: the highest female voice.
entries.definitionCN: 女高音；反义对照。

normalIntro.en: bass is base with a different tail: the low floor of sound, plus a fish that shares only spelling.
normalIntro.cn: bass 是换了尾巴的 base：声音的地板；而鲈鱼只分享拼写。

normal.en: Root: Latin bassus, low.
normal.cn: 词根：拉丁语 bassus「低」。

normal.en: Italian kin: basso.
normal.cn: 意大利同族：basso。

normal.en: Voice: sing bass.
normal.cn: 声部：唱男低音。

normal.en: Fish: sea bass, different origin.
normal.cn: 鱼：海鲈，另有来源。

normal.en: Spot: bass clef marks the low lines.
normal.cn: 谱号：低音谱号标记低音行。

abstract.en: Feel sound you hear with your ribs, not your ears.
abstract.cn: 体会用肋骨而非耳朵去听的声音。

abstract.en: Bass is the gravity of music.
abstract.cn: bass 是音乐里的重力。

abstract.en: A choir without bass is a building without ground.
abstract.cn: 没有男低音的唱诗班，如无地基之楼。

examples.en: The choir's bass held the melody steady.
examples.cn: 唱诗班的男低音稳住了旋律。

examples.en: Freshwater bass thrive in weedy lakes.
examples.cn: 淡水鲈鱼在水草繁茂的湖中繁衍。

examples.en: Her bass guitar anchored the rhythm section.
examples.cn: 她的贝斯撑住了整个节奏组。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝斯」——音译已通行：低音乐器就叫贝斯

root: 音乐义之 bass 出拉丁 bassus「低的」，与 base 同词异拼，受意大利语 basso 影响定形；鲈鱼义之 bass 出古英语 bærs「河鲈」的缩略，两词仅拼写相同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses descend one scale: the low range, the low voice, the low instruments, the fish, the amplifier, the clef, the harmonic floor, and the electric bass.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿音阶下行：低音区、男低音、低音乐器、鲈鱼、音响低频、低音谱号、和声底层与电贝斯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sound floor everything else stands on.
core.cn: 核心意象：其余声音立足其上的声之地板。

branches.en: Range and voice fix the low floor.
branches.cn: 音域与人声钉住低音层。

branches.en: Old and electric instruments serve it.
branches.cn: 传统与电声乐器皆为其服务。

branches.en: Speakers and clefs carry it into rooms and scores.
branches.cn: 音箱与谱号把它带入房间与乐谱。

branches.en: The bass line is harmony's footing.
branches.cn: 贝斯线是和声的地基。

branches.en: The fish swims in by spelling alone.
branches.cn: 鲈鱼仅凭拼写游入本条。

intro.en: The bass family splits at the spelling: one branch hums low, one branch swims.
intro.cn: bass 词族在拼写处分岔：一支低鸣，一支游弋。

latinIntro.en: Latin bassus and Italian basso feed the music branch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bassus 与意大利 basso 喂养音乐一支。

definition_zh: 兽性的；野蛮残忍的；野兽般的；纵欲的；粗鄙堕落的
definition_en: cruel, brutal, or savage like an animal; of or relating to beasts
core_image: 披着人皮的野兽：外表是人，举动却露出獠牙
scene: 他夺走村民的粮食，还烧掉了磨坊，凶残得不像人类。 The invaders committed bestial violence against the villagers.
sceneCN: 这里 bestial 是「野蛮残忍的、兽性的」（第 1 个义项：行为残暴如野兽）；句意是入侵者对村民施加了野兽般的暴行。

pos.zh: 兽性的；残忍的；野兽般的

derivatives.zh: 同源名词，义为「野兽；凶残的人」，bestial 由其派生
bestial 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「兽性；残忍」
bestial 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「野兽般地」
中世纪动物寓言集，同源于拉丁语 bestia

senses.title: Cruel and brutal like an animal
senses.definition: showing cruelty or violence that seems more animal than human
senses.definitionCN: 表现出更像野兽而非人类的残忍或暴力
senses.example: The invaders committed bestial violence against the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵者对村民施加了野兽般的暴行。
senses.why: Latin bestia names the beast, so the core image is a human acting with a beast's ferocity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bestia 指野兽，核心意象是人露出野兽般的凶残。

senses.title: Of or relating to beasts
senses.definition: belonging to or characteristic of animals rather than humans
senses.definitionCN: 属于野兽的，或具有野兽特征的
senses.example: The cave wall showed a bestial figure with horns.
senses.exampleCN: 洞穴壁上画着一个带角的野兽形象。
senses.why: The oldest sense simply points at the beast itself before any judgment of cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项只是指野兽本身，尚无残忍的贬义。

senses.title: Driven by instinct, not reason
senses.definition: governed by appetite or instinct instead of human reason
senses.definitionCN: 受食欲、欲望或本能支配，而不受理智约束
senses.example: Hunger reduced the castaways to a bestial struggle for food.
senses.exampleCN: 饥饿让遇险者们陷入争夺食物的兽性争斗。
senses.why: Beasts live by appetite alone, so stripping away reason leaves the bestial core.
senses.whyCN: 野兽只凭欲望生存，失去理智便只剩兽性内核。

senses.title: Carnal or lustful
senses.definition: expressing crude or excessive sexual appetite
senses.definitionCN: 表现出粗俗或过度的性欲
senses.example: The old play warns against a bestial surrender to desire.
senses.exampleCN: 这出老戏告诫人们不要纵欲无度。
senses.why: Carnal appetite is the animal side of human nature, hence the beast label.
senses.whyCN: 肉欲被视为人性中属于动物的一面，故以野兽相称。

senses.title: Savage in sound or manner
senses.definition: having a raw, animal quality of sound or bearing
senses.definitionCN: 声音或举止带有原始的、野兽般的质感
senses.example: He answered with a bestial growl.
senses.exampleCN: 他兽性大发地吼着回应。
senses.why: The beast image extends from deeds to voice and manner.
senses.whyCN: 野兽的意象从行为延伸到声音和姿态。

senses.title: Degraded and disgusting
senses.definition: shockingly low, filthy, or degrading in condition or conduct
senses.definitionCN: 处境或行为低下、肮脏、令人不齿
senses.example: Prisoners endured bestial living conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯们忍受着非人的生活条件。
senses.why: To live like a beast is to fall beneath ordinary human dignity.
senses.whyCN: 像野兽一样生活，就是跌到人类尊严之下。

senses.title: Greedy and insatiable
senses.definition: marked by a crude, uncontrolled greed
senses.definitionCN: 表现出粗野失控的贪婪
senses.example: A bestial greed for land drove the expansion.
senses.exampleCN: 对土地的野兽般的贪婪推动了扩张。
senses.why: A beast devours without measure, so unbounded greed reads as bestial.
senses.whyCN: 野兽吞食毫无节制，无度的贪婪便被形容为兽性。

senses.title: Dull and brutish (archaic)
senses.definition: lacking human intelligence or feeling, stupid like a beast
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏人类的智慧或情感，愚钝如兽（旧用法）
senses.example: In the old text, the bestial man cannot rise to moral thought.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧文本中，愚钝如兽的人无法进行道德思考。
senses.why: Early writers saw beasts as mindless, so the word once stressed dullness.
senses.whyCN: 早期作家认为野兽无心智，故该词曾有愚钝之义。

intro.en: Bestial comes straight from the Latin word for beast.
intro.cn: bestial 直接来自拉丁语中「野兽」一词。

items.en: bestia meant beast, wild animal; its deeper origin is uncertain, possibly borrowed from an older Mediterranean language.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bestia 意为「野兽、野生动物」；其更深的来源不确定，可能借自更古老的地中海语言。

items.en: bestialis meant of beasts, animal-like.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bestialis 意为「野兽的、像野兽的」。

items.en: bestial passed into Old French with the senses of animal and brutal.
items.cn: bestial 进入古法语，兼有「野兽的」与「残暴的」之义。

items.en: English took the word in the 14th century, chiefly meaning brutal or carnal.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入该词，主要指残暴或纵欲。

items.en: today it stresses savage cruelty, with a technical sense in descriptions of animal nature.
items.cn: 如今它强调野蛮残忍，也可在描述动物性时使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the beast root; the near-meaning group gathers words for savage or animal-like conduct.
note.cn: 形近组共享 beast 词根；近义组汇集野蛮、兽性类词。

entries.definition: an animal, especially a large or dangerous one
entries.definitionCN: 野兽——bestial 的同源名词

entries.definition: a medieval book describing beasts
entries.definitionCN: 动物寓言集——同源于拉丁语 bestia

entries.definition: brutal or animal-like behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 兽性；残忍——bestial 的派生名词

entries.definition: cruel and violent
entries.definitionCN: 野蛮的；残忍的；不强调动物意象

entries.definition: fierce and violent, uncivilized
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛的；未开化的；兼有原始与残暴之意

entries.definition: in a wild state, especially of a tame animal gone wild
entries.definitionCN: 野性的；野化的；侧重动物回归野性

normalIntro.cn: bestial 是 beast（拉丁 bestia）加形容词后缀 -ial。

normal.en: Bestiary is the medieval book of beasts.

normal.en: Bestiality names brutal, animal-like conduct.
normal.cn: bestiality 指兽性的、残忍的行为。

normal.en: Beast itself came through Old French beste.
normal.cn: beast 本身经古法语 beste 进入英语。

abstract.en: See a man in a suit whose shadow has claws.
abstract.cn: 看一个穿西装的人，影子却长着利爪。

abstract.en: Feel the roar come from a human throat.
abstract.cn: 感受吼声从人的喉咙里发出。

abstract.en: Picture appetite running without any rein of reason.
abstract.cn: 想象欲望脱缰狂奔，理智毫无约束。

examples.en: The invaders committed bestial violence against the villagers.
examples.cn: 入侵者对村民施加了野兽般的暴行。

examples.en: Hunger reduced the castaways to a bestial struggle for food.
examples.cn: 饥饿让遇险者们陷入争夺食物的兽性争斗。

examples.en: Prisoners endured bestial living conditions.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「白兽」——表面上白白净净是个人，内里却是头白毛野兽，兽性大发。

sensesIntro.en: From simply belonging to beasts, the word grows into cruelty, appetite, degradation, and even old senses of dullness.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「属于野兽」出发，词义长出残忍、欲望、堕落乃至旧义的愚钝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a human being with the face of a beast
core.cn: 核心意象：长着野兽面孔的人

branches.en: Cruelty in deed and voice
branches.cn: 行为与声音中的残暴

branches.en: The plain animal sense
branches.cn: 单纯的野兽义项

branches.cn: 本能、肉欲与贪婪

intro.cn: bestial 建立在拉丁语「野兽」词根加关系形容词后缀之上。

latinIntro.en: The bestia family in Latin and beyond.

items.structure: English noun, from Old French beste

items.meaningCN: 挚友（现代俚语，同源于 beast）

definition_zh: 为特定用途配置的一整套器械或装置；也可指机构、组织等抽象体系
definition_en: a set of equipment assembled for a particular purpose, or an organized system such as a state or party structure
core_image: 实验台上，玻璃管、支架、气瓶与阀门连成一套，每一段都扣在指定的位置，只为完成一次反应
scene: 潜水前，队员检查背上的气瓶、减压阀与面罩，确认每一处接头都不漏气。 The diver checked the breathing apparatus before the descent.
sceneCN: 这里指成套的呼吸装置（第 2 个义项：为潜水或消防配置的呼吸器）；句意：潜水员在下潜前检查了呼吸装置。
