senses.title: A set assembled for an experiment
senses.titleCN: 为实验组装的一套器械
senses.definition: the connected pieces of equipment set up to carry out a particular experiment or operation
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项实验或操作而连接起来的一套器材
senses.example: The whole apparatus was rebuilt after the glass tube broke.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃管破裂后，整套装置被重新组装。
senses.why: Apparatus names a prepared set, not a single tool, because its root verb means to make ready.
senses.whyCN: 「装置」指准备好的一套，而不是单件工具，因为其词根动词意为「准备」。

senses.title: Breathing gear
senses.definition: the cylinder, regulator and mask that let a person breathe under water, in smoke or at altitude
senses.definitionCN: 让人在水下、烟雾中或高空呼吸的气瓶、调节器与面罩组合
senses.example: Firefighters carry breathing apparatus into every smoke-filled room.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员进入每个烟雾弥漫的房间都携带呼吸器。
senses.why: A life-support set is prepared before entry, so the general word attaches to this specialised kit.
senses.whyCN: 生命维持装备要在进入前准备好，因此这个泛称也附着于这套专用器材。

senses.title: The machinery of an organization
senses.definition: the offices, departments and procedures through which a state, party or large body acts
senses.definitionCN: 国家、政党或大型团体赖以行动的机关、部门与程序
senses.example: The reform aimed at the party apparatus rather than at voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革针对的是政党机构，而不是选民。
senses.why: An organisation acts through prepared parts, so the tool word becomes a metaphor for institutional machinery.
senses.whyCN: 组织通过准备好的各个部件行动，于是工具词变成了机构机械的比喻。

senses.title: Gymnastic equipment
senses.definition: the fixed or portable frames and bars used in gymnastics, such as the rings or parallel bars
senses.definitionCN: 体操中使用的固定或可移动框架与横杆，如吊环或双杠
senses.example: The hall's apparatus was inspected before the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前，馆内的体操器械接受了检查。
senses.why: Sporting equipment is also a prepared set, so the word serves for bars, rings and beams.
senses.whyCN: 运动器材同样是准备好的一套，因此这个词也用于横杆、吊环与平衡木。

senses.title: Optical or measuring setup
senses.definition: a bench of lenses, mirrors, lasers and detectors aligned for one measurement
senses.definitionCN: 为一次测量而对准的透镜、反射镜、激光器与探测器组合
senses.example: The optical apparatus had to stay aligned within a micron.
senses.exampleCN: 这套光学装置必须在微米范围内保持对准。
senses.why: Precision work needs many parts fixed in relation to one another, which is exactly what apparatus means.
senses.whyCN: 精密工作需要许多部件按相对位置固定，这正是「装置」所指。

senses.title: Textual collation notes
senses.definition: the recorded variants and editorial notes that accompany a scholarly edition of a text
senses.definitionCN: 学术版本正文旁记录的异文与编者说明
senses.example: The critical apparatus lists every manuscript reading.
senses.exampleCN: 校勘资料列出了每种抄本的读法。
senses.why: Scholars prepare a text with supporting parts, and the old word for equipment names those supporting notes.
senses.whyCN: 学者为正文准备支撑材料，古老的「装备」一词便用来指这些辅助记录。

senses.title: The assembly of a machine
senses.definition: the connected parts of a machine considered as one working whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一台机器的各连接部件视为一个运作整体
senses.example: The valve is only one part of the pumping apparatus.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门只是泵送装置的一部分。
senses.why: The word can name the whole working assembly, not only a bench setup, whenever the parts act together.
senses.whyCN: 只要部件协同运作，这个词就可指整个工作总成，而不只是台面装置。

senses.title: Darkroom and photographic gear
senses.definition: the enlarger, trays, tanks and safelights used to develop photographs
senses.definitionCN: 用于冲洗照片的放大机、药盘、罐与安全灯
senses.example: The school still keeps a darkroom apparatus behind the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 学校仍在摄影室后面保留着一套暗房器材。
senses.why: A craft that needs a fixed sequence of prepared tools give the word another specialised home.
senses.whyCN: 需要固定工序与预备工具的技艺，又给这个词添了一个专用场所。

intro.en: Apparatus is a Latin noun for equipment, built on a verb meaning to prepare; English borrowed it whole, including its Latin plural.
intro.cn: 「装置」是拉丁语中表示装备的名词，建立在表示「准备」的动词上；英语整体借入，连拉丁语复数形式也一并保留。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare, make ready or furnish; it is the direct Latin source, while its deeper origin is uncertain and the link to a producing root is only a suggestion.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语动词指准备、备好或供给；它是本词的直接拉丁语来源，其更早来源存疑，与表示「产出」之古词根的关联仅为推测。

items.en: The prefix ad-, meaning toward, combined with parare to give apparare, to get ready for a purpose.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀与「准备」结合，构成「为某目的做好准备」的动词。

items.en: Apparatus was the result noun: the state of being prepared and the set of things prepared, especially for a task.
items.cn: 这个词是结果名词，指准备好的状态以及准备好的一套东西，尤指为某项任务所备。

items.en: The Latin fourth-declension noun kept the same form in the plural, and English still allows apparatus as a plural.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语第四变格名词的复数与原形同形，英语至今仍允许用原形作复数。

items.era: ENGLISH BORROWING · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century for a prepared set of instruments, especially in science; the exact year of the borrowing is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个词，指准备好的一套器具，尤用于科学；具体借入年代不确定。

items.en: The same picture of prepared parts was later applied to state and party machinery and to the notes that support an edited text.
items.cn: 同一幅「准备好的部件」画面后来被用于国家与政党机构，以及支撑校勘版本的注释。

note.en: The first group shares the prepare root; the second group separates the four kit words.
note.cn: 第一组共享「准备」词根；第二组区分四个器械名词。

entries.definition: The English plural, used when several separate sets are counted.
entries.definitionCN: 英语复数，用于清点几套分开的装置。

entries.definition: To make ready; the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 做好准备；名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: The act of making ready; it stresses the process, not the set.
entries.definitionCN: 准备的动作；强调过程而非成套之物。

entries.definition: To make ready again; it shares the prepare root with a again-prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 重新备好；共享「准备」词根并带「再次」前缀。

entries.definition: A bought or issued set of machines and tools; apparatus is assembled for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 采购或配发的成套机器工具；装置是为任务组装起来的。

entries.definition: One precision measuring tool; apparatus is the whole setup around it.
entries.definitionCN: 单件精密测量器具；装置是围绕它的整套布置。

entries.definition: The installed system of measuring and control devices in a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 工厂中安装的测量与控制仪表系统。

entries.definition: An improvised or temporary setup; apparatus is more deliberate and complete.
entries.definitionCN: 临时拼搭的装置；目标词更像有意搭成的完整一套。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root verb means to prepare, so apparatus is the set made ready.
normal.cn: 词根动词意为准备，因此装置就是准备好的一套。

normal.en: The family runs prepare, preparation, preparatory, repair and apparatus.
normal.cn: 同族词包括准备、制备、预备的、修理与装置。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: laboratory apparatus, breathing apparatus, state apparatus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：实验装置、呼吸器、国家机构。

normal.en: The Latin plural is the same word, though English also allows apparatuses.
normal.cn: 拉丁语复数与原形同形，英语也允许加复数词尾。

normal.en: Its cousins are equipment, instrument, instrumentation and rig.
normal.cn: 它的近亲是设备、仪器、仪表系统与临时装置。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every glass tube knows exactly where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每根玻璃管都清楚自己该在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a mask that turns a hostile environment into breathable air.
abstract.cn: 想象一副面罩，把恶劣环境变成可呼吸的空气。

abstract.en: Picture a building full of offices acting like one prepared machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋装满办公室的建筑，像一台准备好的机器那样运作。

examples.en: The apparatus must be assembled in the order given in the manual.
examples.cn: 这套装置必须按手册给定的顺序组装。

examples.en: The state apparatus moved faster than the ministry itself.
examples.cn: 国家机构比部委本身行动得更快。

examples.en: A broken seal can ruin an entire breathing apparatus.
examples.cn: 一处密封破损就能毁掉整套呼吸装置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「预先备好」的一整套器械，连复数都沿用拉丁原形

root: 源自拉丁语「为某目的准备」的动词及其结果名词；更早词源不确定，英语十七世纪整体借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: parts prepared and joined for a purpose. The purpose may be an experiment, breathing, sport, measurement, scholarship or the action of an organization.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念：部件为某目的备好并连接起来。这个目的可以是实验、呼吸、运动、测量、校勘，或一个组织的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench of parts clipped into place, each in its fixed position, ready for one operation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台面部件被扣在各自固定位置，为一套操作准备就绪。

branches.en: THE CORE: an assembled set for an experiment, and the working parts of a machine.
branches.cn: 核心：为实验组装的整套器械，以及机器的工作部件。

branches.en: THE LIFE-SUPPORT VERSION: cylinders, regulators and masks.
branches.cn: 生命维持版本：气瓶、调节器与面罩。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL VERSION: the offices and procedures of a state or party.
branches.cn: 机构版本：国家或政党的机关与程序。

branches.en: THE SPORT AND DARKROOM VERSION: rings, bars, enlargers and trays.
branches.cn: 运动与暗房版本：吊环、横杆、放大机与药盘。

branches.en: THE PRECISION AND SCHOLARLY VERSION: aligned optical benches and collation notes.
branches.cn: 精密与学术版本：对准的光学台与校勘注释。

intro.en: The word is wholly Latin: a preparing verb, a purpose prefix and a result noun.
intro.cn: 这个词完全来自拉丁语：一个「准备」动词、一个表目的前缀与一个结果名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin apparare and apparatus supply the form; the plural is the same Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「准备」与「装置」提供了词形；复数沿用同一拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 学费（美式常用）；教学、讲授（英式）；辅导；监护（古义）
definition_en: the money charged for teaching, especially at a college; also the teaching itself, private coaching, or the older sense of guardianship
core_image: 缴费窗口的玻璃后面贴着一行行收费说明，窗前的家长拿着账单核对每一笔
scene: 大学财务处的窗口前，家长拿着账单核对每一行收费，玻璃后面贴着缴费说明，队伍一直排到楼梯口。 Tuition at the state university stayed frozen for three years.
sceneCN: 这里指「学费」（第 1 个义项：高校为教学收取的费用）；句意为这所州立大学的学费连续三年未涨。图中可辨识物件：缴费账单、窗口、收费说明、排队的人群。

pos.zh: 辅导；补习（可指具体课时）

senses.title: The charge for teaching
senses.definition: the money a college or school charges for instruction
senses.definitionCN: 学院或学校为教学收取的费用
senses.example: Tuition at the state university stayed frozen for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这所州立大学的学费连续三年未涨。
senses.why: the word moved from the care of a student to the price of that care, which is now the dominant American sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「对学生的照管」转到「照管的价钱」，这一义如今在美式用法中占主导。

senses.title: Teaching itself
senses.definition: the act or work of teaching, especially to a small group or an individual
senses.definitionCN: 教学或授课的工作，尤指面向小组或个人
senses.example: He gives tuition in mathematics to advanced pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 他为高年级学生讲授数学。
senses.why: the older sense of guardianship narrowed into instruction, and British usage kept that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 「监护」的旧义收窄为「教导」，英式用法保留了这一义。

senses.title: Private coaching
senses.definition: paid one-to-one or small-group teaching outside a school
senses.definitionCN: 在校外进行、收费的一对一或小班教学
senses.example: She pays for weekly tuition in French.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周付费上法语辅导课。
senses.why: when instruction is bought by the hour, the abstract noun becomes a countable service.
senses.whyCN: 当教学按小时购买时，抽象名词就变成可按次计的服务。

senses.title: Guided learning in general
senses.definition: the process of being guided in learning by a more expert person
senses.definitionCN: 由更内行的人引导学习的过程
senses.example: Under his tuition the apprentices learned to read a drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 在他的指导下，学徒们学会了看图纸。
senses.why: the word still carries the warmth of personal guidance rather than mere instruction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词仍带个人引导的温度，而不只是单向讲授。

senses.title: Guardianship
senses.definition: the office of watching over a person or a thing
senses.definitionCN: 看护某人或某物的职责
senses.example: The estate was held in tuition until the heir came of age.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业处于监护之下，直到继承人成年。
senses.why: this is the oldest sense: watching over someone, long before anyone charged for lessons.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：看护某人，远早于有人为授课收费。

senses.title: The total cost of instruction
senses.titleCN: 学费总额；教育开支（引申）
senses.definition: the whole sum a family spends on instruction over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一个家庭在一段时间内为教学支出的总额
senses.example: Four years of tuition consumed most of their savings.
senses.exampleCN: 四年的学费花掉了他们大部分积蓄。
senses.why: the price sense was extended from a single charge to the whole bill.
senses.whyCN: 价钱义从单笔收费扩展到整张账单。

senses.title: The charge for one course
senses.definition: the amount charged for a particular course or module
senses.definitionCN: 为某门课程或模块收取的费用
senses.example: Tuition for the evening module is billed separately.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间模块的学费单独计费。
senses.why: the price sense narrows to a single module when billing separates one course from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 计费把一门课单独列出时，价钱义就收窄到单个模块。

senses.title: Any price paid to learn
senses.titleCN: 比喻：为学到东西付出的代价
senses.definition: whatever one must give up in order to gain knowledge or skill
senses.definitionCN: 为获得知识或技能而必须付出的任何东西
senses.example: The mistakes were the tuition he paid for experience.
senses.exampleCN: 那些错误就是他换取经验所付的学费。
senses.why: the money image is borrowed: what is paid can be money, time or suffering.
senses.whyCN: 货币意象被借用：付出的可以是钱、时间或痛苦。

intro.en: Tuition comes from Latin tuitio 'a watching over, protection', from tueri 'to guard'; the teaching sense grew out of guardianship.
intro.cn: tuition 出自拉丁 tuitio「看护、保护」，其动词为 tueri「守护」；教学义由监护义生长出来。

items.en: Tueri meant 'to watch over, guard, keep safe', used of persons, property and even crops.
items.cn: tueri 意为「看守、守护、保全」，对象可以是人、财产甚至庄稼。

items.en: Tuitio, the noun of action, named a watching over, hence protection and guardianship.
items.cn: 动作名词 tuitio 指看护这一行为，因此有保护与监护之义。

items.en: Old French tuition carried the same legal and protective meaning into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 tuition 带着同样的法律与保护含义，在十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Early English tuition meant guardianship and protection, with no connection to fees.
items.cn: 早期英语中这个词指监护与保护，与收费毫无关系。

items.en: By the sixteenth century it named instruction, and by the nineteenth the American price sense had become standard.
items.cn: 到十六世纪它已指教导；到十九世纪，美式的「价钱」义成为标准用法。

items.en: Dating note: the date of the shift from guardianship to instruction is approximate, and no single document marks the change.
items.cn: 年代说明：从监护到教导的转变年代只是约数，没有单一文献标记这次变化。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same guarding root; group two holds other words for teaching and its price.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「守护」词根的词；第二组是其他表示教学及其价钱的词。

entries.definition: One who guards and guides a learner; the person behind the instruction.
entries.definitionCN: 看护并引导学习者的人；教学背后的人。

entries.definition: A small teaching session, often one-to-one; it names the event, not the charge.
entries.definitionCN: 小规模教学时段，常为一对一；指事件，不指收费。

entries.definition: The state of being under a guardian or a teacher; the oldest sense of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 处于监护人或教师之下的状态；这一族里最古老的义项。

entries.definition: From a related Latin verb meaning 'to look at', so it shares the guarding root but means direct knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自同源拉丁动词「观看」，与「守护」词根相关，但指直觉认知。

entries.definition: The money charged for a service; tuition is the service or the whole charge, a fee is one payment.
entries.definitionCN: 为服务收取的钱；该词指服务或总费用，单笔付款另有一词。

entries.definition: The act of teaching; it does not carry the guardianship history or the price.
entries.definitionCN: 教学行为；不带监护的历史，也不带价钱义。

entries.definition: Targeted training for a skill or an exam; narrower than tuition.
entries.definitionCN: 针对技能或考试的专门训练，比该词窄。

entries.definition: Education received at school; it names the whole process rather than paid lessons.
entries.definitionCN: 在学校接受的教育；指整个历程而非付费课程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real billing phrases and real offices.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词根、真实缴费搭配与真实财务窗口。

normal.en: The root means to guard: guarding a learner became guiding a learner, and guiding acquired a price.
normal.cn: 词根意为守护：守护学生变成引导学生，引导又添上了价钱。

normal.en: The family runs tutor, tutorial, tutelage and tuition fee.
normal.cn: 同一词族包括导师、辅导课、监护与学费。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: pay tuition, tuition costs, private tuition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：缴学费、学费开支、私人辅导。

normal.en: British usage keeps the teaching sense; American usage keeps the price sense.
normal.cn: 英式保留教学义，美式保留价钱义。

normal.en: Picture the bursar's window: the same word for the lesson and the bill.
normal.cn: 想象财务处的窗口：课与账单用的是同一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a guard at a gate who slowly becomes a guide at a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象门口的守卫慢慢变成桌旁的指导者。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt that lists hours instead of goods.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据，上面列的是课时而不是货物。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge toll paid in effort rather than coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥的过路费，用力气而不是硬币支付。

examples.en: Tuition at the state university stayed frozen for three years.
examples.cn: 这所州立大学的学费连续三年未涨。

examples.en: He gives tuition in mathematics to advanced pupils.
examples.cn: 他为高年级学生讲授数学。

examples.en: She pays for weekly tuition in French.
examples.cn: 她每周付费上法语辅导课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「守护」慢慢变成「教」，「教」又要付钱 → 学费

root: 拉丁 tuitio「看护、保护」，其动词 tueri 意为「守护」；由「守护学生」引申为「教导」，再引申为「为教导支付的费用」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses trace one transfer of care: guarding a person, then guiding a learner, then charging for the guidance, then extending the charge to a course, a year, a whole education and finally to any price paid to learn.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一次「照管」的转移：先守护一个人，再引导一个学习者，再为引导收费，再把收费扩展到一门课、一年、整段教育，最后扩展到任何为学习付出的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bursar's window, where the word for a lesson and the word for a bill are printed on the same glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：财务处的窗口，教学的字样与账单的数额印在同一块玻璃上。

branches.en: PRICE AND METAPHOR: the actual charge, then any cost paid in time or pain.
branches.cn: 价钱与比喻：先是真实的收费，再是任何以时间或痛苦支付的代价。

branches.en: TEACHING: group instruction, bought coaching, and guided learning in general.
branches.cn: 教学：集体讲授、按次购买的辅导，以及一般的引导性学习。

branches.en: PRIVATE HOURS: instruction sold by the session rather than by the year.
branches.cn: 私人课时：按次而非按年出售的教学。

branches.en: THE OLDEST SENSE: guardianship, before any fee existed.
branches.cn: 最古义项：收费出现之前的监护。

branches.en: SCALE: one course billed apart, then four years summed into one figure.
branches.cn: 规模：先是一门课单独计费，再把四年合成一个数字。

intro.en: Tuition is a Latin noun of action whose root also gives tutor, tutorial and tutelage; the family is about watching over.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动作名词，其词根还构成导师、辅导课与监护；整族词的核心都是「看护」。

latinIntro.en: Latin tueri 'to guard' gives tuition, tutor, tutelage and tutelary; tuitio is the noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tueri「守护」衍生出 tuition、tutor、tutelage 与 tutelary；tuitio 是它的动作名词。

items.example: The root carries the idea of keeping someone safe.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着保护某人的意思。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The ending turns the guarding verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把守护的动词变成名词。

items.meaning: a watching over; later, instruction and its price
items.meaningCN: 看护；后指教导及其价钱
items.example: Tuition now mostly means the price of teaching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词如今多指教学的价钱。

items.example: A tutor meets the student twice a week.
items.exampleCN: 导师每周与学生见两次。

items.example: Under her tutelage he learned the trade.
items.exampleCN: 在她的指导之下，他学会了这门手艺。

items.example: The Latin noun began as a legal protection.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词最初是法律意义上的保护。

items.example: The tuition fee is due in August.

definition_zh: 生理学；生理机能；（某生物或某系统的）生理特性
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies how living systems function, or the functions themselves
core_image: 一间实验室里，跑步机连着呼吸面罩，屏幕上跳动的曲线记录身体在运动时如何耗氧
scene: 运动生理实验室里，研究员看着屏幕说： Physiology explains why the runner's heart rate climbs so quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 physiology 指「研究生命系统如何运作的生理学」（第 1 个义项：研究身体机能的学科）；句意是生理学解释了这位跑者心率为何升得这么快。

senses.title: The science of how living systems work
senses.titleCN: 研究生命系统如何运作的学科
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies the functions of living organisms and their parts
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体及其各部位功能的生物学分支
senses.example: Physiology explains why the runner's heart rate climbs so quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 生理学解释了这位跑者心率为何升得这么快。
senses.why: Physis is nature and -logia is study; the word began as an inquiry into nature and narrowed to the functions of living bodies.
senses.whyCN: physis 是「自然」，-logia 是「研究」；这个词最初指对自然的探究，后来收窄为对生命体机能的探究。

senses.title: The functions themselves
senses.definition: the actual functioning of a living organism or system
senses.definitionCN: 生命体或系统实际的运作方式
senses.example: The physiology of the diving seal conserves oxygen for long periods.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水海豹的生理机能可长时间保存氧气。
senses.why: Like morphology, the noun can name the object of study rather than the study, so physiology also means the functioning itself.
senses.whyCN: 与 morphology 一样，这个名词也可指研究对象而非学科，因此 physiology 也指运作本身。

senses.title: The functional traits of one organism
senses.titleCN: 某一生物特有的生理特性
senses.definition: the particular functional characteristics of a given species or individual
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种或个体特有的功能特征
senses.example: The physiology of this cactus suits a desert with rare rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这种仙人掌的生理特性适应少雨的沙漠。
senses.why: The word narrows from the general science to the specific set of functions that makes one organism suited to its life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从普通学科收窄为某一生物适应其生活的一套具体机能。

senses.title: Plant physiology as a branch
senses.titleCN: 作为分支的植物生理学
senses.definition: the study of how plants take up water, make food and respond to their environment
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物如何吸水、制造养分并回应环境的分支
senses.example: Plant physiology studies how roots sense drought before leaves wilt.
senses.exampleCN: 植物生理学研究根如何在叶片萎蔫之前察觉干旱。
senses.why: Each kingdom gets its own physiology, because plants solve the same problems with different machinery.
senses.whyCN: 每个生物界都有自己的生理学，因为植物用不同机制解决同样的问题。

senses.title: Exercise physiology as a branch
senses.titleCN: 作为分支的运动生理学
senses.definition: the study of how the body responds and adapts to physical activity
senses.definitionCN: 研究身体如何回应并适应体育活动的分支
senses.example: Exercise physiology measures oxygen uptake during a sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 运动生理学测量短跑时的摄氧量。
senses.why: When muscles are pushed, the functions become measurable, and a whole applied branch grows around that setting.
senses.whyCN: 当肌肉受到推动时，机能变得可测量，一整个应用分支便围绕这一情境生长出来。

senses.title: Cell physiology
senses.definition: the study of the functions of cells and their membranes
senses.definitionCN: 研究细胞及其膜功能的学问
senses.example: Cell physiology asks how ions cross a membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞生理学追问离子如何穿过细胞膜。
senses.why: The same word scales down to the cell, where function means transport, signalling and metabolism.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词可缩小到细胞尺度，那里的功能指运输、信号与代谢。

senses.title: Comparative physiology
senses.definition: the study of functional differences across species
senses.definitionCN: 研究不同物种之间功能差异的学问
senses.example: Comparative physiology shows how the same organ works at different temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 比较生理学显示同一器官在不同温度下如何运作。
senses.why: Comparing functions across species turns physiology into an evolutionary tool as well as a medical one.
senses.whyCN: 跨物种比较功能，使生理学既是医学工具，也是演化工具。

senses.title: The functioning of one body system
senses.definition: the functional behaviour of a particular organ or system
senses.definitionCN: 某一器官或系统的功能表现
senses.example: Cardiac physiology covers the filling and pumping of the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏生理学涵盖心脏的充盈与泵血。
senses.why: Any organ can be given its own physiology, since each has a set of jobs that can be described on its own.
senses.whyCN: 任何器官都可以有自己的生理学，因为每个器官都有一组可单独描述的工作。

intro.en: Physiology comes from Latin physiologia, from Greek physiologia, an inquiry into nature, built on physis nature and -logia study; the modern medical sense is later and narrower.
intro.cn: physiology 来自拉丁 physiologia，再上溯希腊 physiologia「对自然的探究」，由 physis「自然」与 -logia「研究」构成；现代医学义更晚、更窄。

items.en: Physis meant nature or the essential character of a thing; it derives from phyein to grow, and the deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: physis 意为自然或事物的本性；它来自 phyein「生长」，更深的印欧语形式属重构形式。

items.en: Phyein meant to bring forth, grow or spring up; the idea of growth underlies the word for nature.
items.cn: phyein 意为产生、生长、萌发；生长的观念构成「自然」一词的基础。

items.en: Logia, from logos, named the study or account of a subject.
items.cn: logia 出自 logos，指对某主题的研究或论述。

items.en: Latin took the Greek compound as physiologia, still meaning inquiry into nature rather than medicine.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这一希腊复合词作 physiologia，仍指对自然的探究，而非医学。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the late sixteenth century; the narrower sense of bodily functions became dominant in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪晚期借入该词；到 19 世纪，指身体机能的较窄义成为主导。

items.era: UNCERTAIN DETAILS (DATE APPROXIMATE, DEEP ROOT RECONSTRUCTED)
items.en: Source uncertain only in detail: the first English date is approximate, and any Indo-European base for phyein is a reconstruction; the Greek compound itself is well attested.
items.cn: 来源仅在细节上不确定：英语首见年代为约数，phyein 的任何印欧语基形式均属重构；希腊复合词本身有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Greek nature root that are often confused with physiology; group two holds neighbouring life-science disciplines.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「自然」词根、常与 physiology 混淆的词；第二组是相邻的生命科学学科。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to body functions; it describes a trait, while physiology names the field or the functions.
entries.definitionCN: 表示与身体机能有关的形容词；它描述性状，而 physiology 指学科或机能本身。

entries.definition: A person who studies physiology; the -ist suffix turns the field into its practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生理学的人；-ist 后缀把学科变成从业者。

entries.definition: The form and build of a body, from the same Greek nature root but focusing on shape rather than function.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形貌与体格，同出希腊「自然」词根，但侧重形状而非功能。

entries.definition: The science of matter and energy, from Greek physika natural things; it shares the root but studies non-living systems.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量的科学，来自希腊 physika「自然之物」；共享词根，但研究非生命系统。

entries.definition: The study of life in general; physiology is one of its branches.
entries.definitionCN: 对生命的一般研究；生理学是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: The study of body structure; it supplies the parts that physiology explains the workings of.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体结构的学问；它提供部件，生理学解释这些部件如何运作。

entries.definition: The job a part performs; physiology is the systematic study of such jobs.
entries.definitionCN: 某部件所执行的工作；生理学是对这些工作的系统研究。

entries.definition: The chemistry of living systems; it explains many mechanisms that physiology describes at the body level.
entries.definitionCN: 生命系统的化学；它解释许多生理学在身体层面描述的机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Physis nature plus -logia study: the study of how living nature works.
normal.cn: physis「自然」加 -logia「研究」：研究活的自然如何运作。

normal.en: The family runs physiology, physiological, physiologist, physiologically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 physiology、physiological、physiologist、physiologically。

normal.en: Exercise, plant, comparative and cardiac physiology are fixed branches.
normal.cn: 运动、植物、比较与心脏生理学是固定分支。

normal.en: Anatomy gives the parts; physiology gives the workings.
normal.cn: 解剖学给出部件；生理学给出运作方式。

normal.en: The word narrowed from all of nature to living bodies.
normal.cn: 这个词从整个自然收窄到生命体。

abstract.en: Picture a dashboard of dials, each recording one body process.
abstract.cn: 想象一块仪表盘，每个表盘记录一项身体过程。

abstract.en: Picture a city's utility maps showing water, power and waste at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市的管线图，同时显示水、电与废物。

abstract.en: Picture a machine whose manual explains only what each part does, never what it is made of.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器的手册只解释每个部件做什么，从不讲它由什么构成。

examples.en: She teaches physiology to first-year medical students.
examples.cn: 她给一年级医学生讲授生理学。

examples.en: The physiology of high-altitude birds has been studied for decades.
examples.cn: 高原鸟类的生理学已被研究数十年。

examples.en: His paper links physiology with behaviour in ants.
examples.cn: 他的论文把蚂蚁的生理与行为联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「physio 自然/身体 + ology 学科」——研究身体如何运作 → 生理学

root: 拉丁 physiologia，出自希腊 physiologia「对自然的探究」= physis「自然」（来自 phyein「生长」）+ -logia「研究」；更深印欧语基为重构形式，英语首见年代约 16 世纪晚期。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole science to the functions it studies, then to one organism, one branch, one setting, one cell and one organ.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整门学科走向它所研究的机能，再走向单个生物、单个分支、单个情境、单个细胞与单个器官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body on a treadmill, wired to dials that turn invisible workings into visible curves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体在跑步机上接着仪表，把看不见的运作变成可见的曲线。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND OBJECT: physiology is both the study of function and the function studied.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：生理学既是研究机能的学问，也是被研究的机能。

branches.en: ONE ORGANISM: a species carries its own set of working arrangements.
branches.cn: 单个生物：每个物种带着自己的一套运作安排。

branches.en: APPLIED BRANCHES: plants and athletes pose different functional questions.
branches.cn: 应用分支：植物与运动员提出不同的功能问题。

branches.en: SCALES: the same word covers a cell membrane and a whole heart.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一个词覆盖细胞膜与整颗心脏。

branches.en: COMPARISON: putting species side by side turns function into evidence for evolution.
branches.cn: 比较：把物种并排摆开，功能便成为演化证据。

intro.en: Physiology is a Greek compound whose parts recur in medicine and biology, so the word can be read as nature plus study.
intro.cn: physiology 是一个希腊复合词，其部件在医学与生物学中反复出现，因此可按「自然 + 研究」读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek physis and phyein give physics, physique and physiology; Greek logos gives -logia and the names of disciplines.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 physis 与 phyein 衍生 physics、physique 与 physiology；希腊 logos 衍生 -logia 及学科名称。

items.example: The root survives in physics and physiology.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根存留于 physics 与 physiology 中。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of growth inside nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为「自然」注入生长的观念。

items.example: The suffix names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门研究领域。

items.example: Latin borrowed the word unchanged in sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语原样借入这个词，意义未变。
生理学家测量了摄氧量。

items.meaning: the science of matter and energy
items.exampleCN: 物理学研究非生命物质。

items.example: The athlete has a powerful physique.

definition_zh: n. 双语能力；双语现象；（国家的）双语制度
definition_en: the ability to use two languages; the practice of using two languages in a country or a school
core_image: 一个人在同一天里，上午用母语开会，下午用另一种语言点咖啡
scene: 在双语家庭长大的孩子自然而然地拥有双语能力。 Children raised in a bilingual household develop bilingualism naturally.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bilingualism 指使用两种语言的能力；句意是在双语家庭长大的孩子自然具备双语能力。

forms.label: 不可数名词（一般无复数）

senses.title: The ability to use two languages
senses.definition: the state of being able to speak and understand two languages
senses.definitionCN: 能够说并理解两种语言的状态
senses.example: Her bilingualism opened doors in two job markets.
senses.exampleCN: 她的双语能力为她打开了两边的就业市场。
senses.why: The suffix -ism turns the adjective bilingual into the name of a condition or ability.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 把形容词 bilingual 变成一种状态或能力的名称。

senses.title: A policy of two official languages
senses.definition: an official arrangement in which two languages are used in public life
senses.definitionCN: 公共生活中同时使用两种语言的正式安排
senses.example: Official bilingualism shapes every sign in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 官方双语制度决定了首都每一块标牌的写法。
senses.why: The same noun names both what a person has and what a state practises.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指个人拥有的能力，也指国家实行的制度。

intro.en: Bilingualism is Latin bi-, two, plus lingua, tongue, plus the noun ending -ismus.
intro.cn: bilingualism 是拉丁语 bi-（二）加 lingua（舌头、语言），再加名词词尾 -ismus。

items.en: Lingua means tongue and, by extension, a language.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头，引申为语言。

items.en: Bilinguis describes someone with two tongues.
items.cn: bilinguis 形容「有两条舌头」的人。

items.en: English bilingual names a person or text in two languages.
items.cn: 英语 bilingual 指使用两种语言的人或双语文本。

items.en: The -ism noun names the condition rather than the person.
items.cn: 加 -ism 的名词指状态，而不是人。

items.en: Schools adopt the word for teaching through two languages.
items.cn: 学校用这个词指用两种语言授课。

items.en: Official bilingualism becomes a term of law and politics.
items.cn: 官方双语成为法律与政治术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bi- or -ism shape; the near-meaning group counts how many languages are in play.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bi- 或 -ism 的形状；近义组按涉及的语言数量排列。

entries.definition: Using two languages.
entries.definitionCN: 使用两种语言的。

entries.definition: A sound made with both lips.
entries.definitionCN: 双唇发出的音。

entries.definition: Every two months or twice a month.
entries.definitionCN: 两月一次或一月两次的。

entries.definition: Having two poles or extremes.
entries.definitionCN: 有两极或两种极端的。

entries.definition: The use of a single language.
entries.definitionCN: 只使用一种语言。

entries.definition: The use of several languages.
entries.definitionCN: 使用多种语言。

entries.definition: Two varieties of one language used for different purposes.

normalIntro.en: Lingua is tongue, so bilingualism is literally having two tongues at your service.
normalIntro.cn: lingua 是舌头，所以 bilingualism 字面就是「有两条舌头可用」。

normal.en: Lingua means tongue, as in linguistics and language.
normal.cn: lingua 意为舌头，如 linguistics 与 language。

normal.en: Bi- adds two, so bilingual means two tongues.
normal.cn: bi- 加上二，bilingual 就是两条舌头。

normal.en: -ism turns the ability into a name.
normal.cn: -ism 把这种能力变成一个名称。

normal.en: One person, two languages, a whole working day.
normal.cn: 一个人，两种语言，一整天的工作。

normal.en: One country, two official tongues, and the word still fits.
normal.cn: 一个国家，两种官方语言，这个词同样适用。

abstract.en: Two doors into the same room.
abstract.cn: 通往同一个房间的两扇门。

abstract.en: Two dictionaries living in one head.
abstract.cn: 住在同一个脑袋里的两本词典。

abstract.en: A tongue that changes coat by the hour.
abstract.cn: 每小时换一件外衣的舌头。

examples.en: Research links bilingualism with better attention control.
examples.cn: 研究把双语能力与更好的注意力控制联系起来。

examples.en: Official bilingualism requires every form in two languages.
examples.cn: 官方双语制度要求每张表格都有两种语言版本。

examples.en: Her bilingualism came from a childhood split between two cities.
examples.cn: 她的双语能力来自在两个城市之间度过的童年。

sensesIntro.en: The noun has two faces: a skill inside one head, and a rule inside one state.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词有两副面孔：一个人头脑里的技能，以及一个国家里的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one speaker moving all day between two languages without noticing the switch
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个人整天在两种语言间来回，却察觉不到切换

branches.en: A morning meeting in one tongue.
branches.cn: 用一种语言开的早会。

branches.en: Coffee ordered in the other by noon.

branches.en: Road signs printed twice.

branches.en: A parliament with two microphones.
branches.cn: 备着两支麦克风的议会。

branches.en: Two languages held as ordinary equipment.
branches.cn: 把两种语言当作日常装备。

intro.en: Bilingualism is a numeric prefix, a Latin tongue, and a noun ending; the list below builds the whole family of language-count words.
intro.cn: bilingualism 由数字前缀、拉丁语「舌头」和名词词尾构成；下面列出整族「数语言」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua is tongue, bilinguis is two-tongued, and loqui is to speak.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 意为舌头，bilinguis 意为双舌的，loqui 意为说话。

latinEntries.exampleCN: lingua 产生 language 与 linguistics。

definition_zh: 微生物；肉眼不可见、需借助显微镜观察的生物
definition_en: a living thing so small that it can be seen only with a microscope
core_image: 一滴池塘水里挤满肉眼看不见的小生命，放大后显出球状、杆状与螺旋状的轮廓
scene: 这里指「微生物」。 A single microorganism in the pond water can start a whole bloom once nutrients rise.
sceneCN: 这里 microorganism 是「微生物」（第 1 个义项：需用显微镜观察的微小生物）；句意：养分升高后，池塘水里的一个微生物就能引发整片水华。图中可辨识物件：水滴、显微镜视野、成片变绿的水面。

pos.zh: 微生物（可数名词，复数 microorganisms；涵盖细菌、古菌、原生生物、真菌等微小生物）

derivatives.zh: 微生物（带连字符的旧式拼写）
微生物区系；某处的微生物群落
微生物组；微生物群落基因组

senses.title: A Microscopic Living Thing
senses.titleCN: 微生物：小到需显微镜才可见
senses.definition: a living thing too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye
senses.definitionCN: 小到肉眼无法清楚看见的生物
senses.example: Each drop of pond water holds thousands of microorganisms.
senses.exampleCN: 每一滴池塘水里都含有成千上万个微生物。
senses.why: The word joins micro-, 'small', to organism, 'living body'. The defining picture is not a particular shape but a scale: the creature is below the resolving power of the eye.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「小」的 micro- 与表示「生物体」的 organism 合成；它的核心画面不是某个特定形状，而是尺度：小到超出眼睛的分辨能力。

senses.title: A Unicellular Form
senses.titleCN: 单细胞形态：一个细胞就是一个个体
senses.definition: a organism consisting of a single cell
senses.definitionCN: 由一个细胞构成的生物
senses.example: A microorganism such as an amoeba lives as one cell.
senses.exampleCN: 像变形虫这样的微生物以一个细胞的形式生活。
senses.why: Most microorganisms are unicellular: one cell performs every function of life. The sense marks body plan rather than size, though the two usually coincide.
senses.whyCN: 大多数微生物是单细胞的：一个细胞承担全部生命功能；这个义项标出的是身体构造，而不是大小，尽管两者通常同时成立。

senses.title: A Broad Taxonomic Cover
senses.titleCN: 分类上的宽泛覆盖：不止细菌
senses.definition: the loose group covering bacteria, archaea, protists and fungi, and sometimes viruses
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖细菌、古菌、原生生物与真菌，有时也包括病毒的宽泛类别
senses.example: The term microorganism covers both bacteria and single-celled fungi.
senses.exampleCN: 「微生物」这一术语既涵盖细菌，也包括单细胞真菌。
senses.why: Microorganism is not a taxonomic rank; it is a convenience class defined by size. That is why it can hold several unrelated kingdoms, and why virologists debate whether viruses belong.
senses.whyCN: microorganism 不是分类层级，而是按大小划分的方便类别；因此它能容纳几个互不相关的界，也因此病毒学家会争论病毒是否算在内。

senses.title: A Soil Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 土壤微生物：地下循环的工人
senses.definition: a microorganism living in soil and driving its nutrient cycles
senses.definitionCN: 生活在土壤中并驱动土壤养分循环的微生物
senses.example: A soil microorganism released phosphorus from the dead leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一种土壤微生物从枯叶中释放出磷。
senses.why: In soil the word usually names a decomposer or a symbiont. The scale sense recedes and the ecological job comes forward: the organism is defined by what it does in the ground.
senses.whyCN: 在土壤语境中，这个词通常指分解者或共生者；尺度义退后，生态职能走上前，生物体靠它在地里所做的事来定义。

senses.title: A Marine Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 海洋微生物：水体中的微小生产者
senses.definition: a microorganism living in seawater, often a primary producer
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海水中、常为初级生产者的微生物
senses.example: Marine microorganisms produce a large share of the oxygen we breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋微生物产生了我们呼吸的氧气中的很大一部分。
senses.why: In the sea, microscopic algae and bacteria carry out photosynthesis and form the base of the food web. The word then points to a functional layer of the ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: 在海洋中，微小藻类与细菌进行光合作用，构成食物网的基础；此时这个词指向生态系统中的一个功能层。

senses.title: A Pathogenic Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 病原微生物：引起疾病的那一类
senses.definition: a microorganism that causes disease in a host
senses.definitionCN: 能在宿主中引起疾病的微生物
senses.example: The outbreak was traced to a pathogenic microorganism in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 疫情被追溯至水中的一种病原微生物。
senses.why: Here the neutral scale word takes on the medical role. The sense is narrower than S1 because only some microorganisms cause disease, and the speaker is naming that subset.
senses.whyCN: 这里中性的尺度词带上了医学角色；该义项比第 1 个义项窄，因为只有部分微生物致病，说话人指的是这个子集。

senses.title: A Useful Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 有益微生物：发酵与生产中的帮手
senses.definition: a microorganism used for fermentation or industrial production
senses.definitionCN: 用于发酵或工业生产的微生物
senses.example: A beneficial microorganism turns milk into yoghurt overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一种有益微生物一夜之间把牛奶变成酸奶。
senses.why: Humans have long used microorganisms as tools. The sense shifts from 'what it is' to 'what it is good for', and it explains the everyday phrase beneficial microorganism.
senses.whyCN: 人类早已把微生物当作工具；这个义项从「它是什么」转向「它有什么用」，也解释了「有益微生物」这一日常说法。

senses.title: An Indicator Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 指示微生物：用来判断水质或卫生
senses.definition: a microorganism whose presence signals contamination or a condition
senses.definitionCN: 其存在能提示污染或某种状况的微生物
senses.example: The lab counts an indicator microorganism to judge water safety.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室计数一种指示微生物来判断水的安全性。
senses.why: Public health cannot test every pathogen, so it watches a proxy. The indicator is chosen because it is easy to detect and travels the same way as the dangerous ones.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生无法检测每一种病原，于是监测一个替身；被选作指示者的微生物易于检出，且与危险病原走同一条传播路径。

intro.en: Microorganism is a nineteenth-century compound of two Greek-derived elements: micro-, 'small', and organism, 'living body'. The word dates from the great expansion of microscopy and germ theory.
intro.cn: microorganism 是十九世纪由两个希腊来源成分构成的复合词：micro-「小」与 organism「生物体」。它诞生于显微镜技术与病菌学说大发展的年代。

items.en: Greek mikros, the Attic form of smikros, meant 'small, little, petty'. Its Latinized combining form micro- became the standard prefix for 'small' in scientific English. Beekes considers the Greek word possibly Pre-Greek, so its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 mikros（阿提卡方言形式 smikros）意为「小的、微小的」；其拉丁化组合形式 micro- 成为科学英语中表示「小」的标准前缀。Beekes 认为这个希腊词可能来自前希腊语底层，因此其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Organism is recorded from the 1660s for 'organic structure'; the sense 'living animal or plant' appears by 1825, translating German Organismus. It rests on Greek organon 'tool, instrument', literally 'that with which one works'.
items.cn: organism 于十七世纪六十年代记录为「有机结构」，到 1825 年才出现「活的动物或植物」这一义项，译自德语 Organismus。其基础是希腊语 organon「工具、器具」，字面意为「用来工作的东西」。

items.en: Microorganism is recorded from 1855, with the hyphenated micro-organism appearing in the same period. The compound was formed in English rather than borrowed whole from another language.
items.cn: microorganism 记录于 1855 年，带连字符的 micro-organism 也出现在同一时期；这个复合词是在英语内部构成的，而不是从其他语言整体借入。

items.en: The word spread as improved lenses let naturalists see a world below the eye. Pasteur and Koch then linked particular microorganisms to particular diseases, giving the neutral word a medical charge.
items.cn: 随着透镜改进，博物学者看见了一个肉眼以下的世界，这个词随之传播；随后巴斯德与科赫把特定微生物与特定疾病联系起来，使这个中性词带上了医学色彩。

items.en: Viruses are smaller still and cannot reproduce without a host cell. Because they lack independent life, many authors exclude them from microorganisms, while others keep them in the loose class. The boundary is a matter of convention, not of etymology.
items.cn: 病毒更小，且离开宿主细胞无法繁殖；由于不具备独立生命，许多作者把它排除在微生物之外，也有人把它留在这个宽泛类别里。这条边界是约定问题，不是词源问题。

items.en: Recent science added microbiome and microbiota, which name whole communities rather than single cells. Microorganism now sits at the level of the individual, beside these collective terms.
items.cn: 近年的科学又加入了 microbiome 与 microbiota，它们命名的是整个群落而非单个细胞；于是 microorganism 现在处在个体的层次，与这些集体术语并列。

note.en: The first group holds spellings and derivatives built on the same compound. The second group holds everyday and technical words for small life that overlap without being equivalent.
note.cn: 第一组是同一复合词上的拼写变体与派生词；第二组是与「微小生命」相关、彼此重叠但并不等同的日常词与技术词。

entries.definition: The older British spelling with a hyphen. It means exactly the same thing and follows the nineteenth-century habit of hyphenating new compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 带连字符的英式旧拼写，意义完全相同，遵循十九世纪给新复合词加连字符的习惯。

entries.definition: The usual adjective meaning 'of microbes'. It is built on microbe rather than directly on microorganism.
entries.definitionCN: 常用形容词，意为「微生物的」；它建立在 microbe 上，而不是直接建立在 microorganism 上。

entries.definition: The study of microorganisms. The ending -logy marks a discipline, so it is not a word for a living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究微生物的学科；词尾 -logy 表示学科，因此它不是指某种生物的词。

entries.definition: A popular nineteenth-century word for a very small living thing, especially a disease-causing one. It is warmer and less formal than microorganism.
entries.definitionCN: 十九世纪的通俗词，指极小的生物、尤指致病者；比 microorganism 更口语、更不正式。

entries.definition: An everyday word for a microbe that may cause disease. It carries no scientific information about cell type or kingdom.
entries.definitionCN: 日常词，指可能致病的微生物；不包含关于细胞类型或生物界的科学信息。

entries.definition: One kind of microorganism only. Microorganism is the wider term and can cover fungi and protists that bacterium cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 只指其中一类微生物；microorganism 是更宽的词，能涵盖 bacterium 无法涵盖的真菌与原生生物。

entries.definition: Any disease-causing agent, including viruses and parasitic worms. It names a role, while microorganism names a size class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何致病因子，包括病毒与寄生蠕虫；它命名的是角色，而 microorganism 命名的是尺度类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: micro- 'small' + organism 'living body': a living body too small to see.
normal.cn: micro-「小」+ organism「生物体」：小到看不见的生物体。

normal.en: The word is a size class, not a family: bacteria, protists and fungi can all be microorganisms.
normal.cn: 这个词是尺度类别，不是科属：细菌、原生生物与真菌都可以是微生物。

normal.en: The family runs microorganism, microorganisms, micro-organism, microbial, microbiology, microbiota and microbiome.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microorganism、microorganisms、micro-organism、microbial、microbiology、microbiota、microbiome。

normal.en: Collocations mark the habitat: soil, marine, pathogenic, beneficial and indicator microorganisms.
normal.cn: 搭配标出生境：土壤、海洋、病原、有益与指示微生物。

normal.en: A microorganism is defined by scale; a pathogen is defined by harm. The two labels can meet in one cell.
normal.cn: microorganism 按尺度定义，pathogen 按危害定义，两个标签可以落在同一个细胞上。

abstract.en: Picture a whole forest, with predators and prey, living inside one drop of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片森林连同捕食者与猎物，住在一滴水里面。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so small that a single lens must stand in for your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象一群小生命，小到必须用一枚镜片代替你的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a worker invisible to the boss who depends on it every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个老板看不见的工人，而老板每天都依赖他。

examples.en: A microorganism in the milk turned it sour before the morning.
examples.cn: 牛奶中的一种微生物在天亮前就让它变酸了。

examples.en: The team sampled the soil to count every microorganism in a gram.
examples.cn: 团队采集土壤样本，统计每克中的微生物数量。

examples.en: No microorganism was found in the sealed water sample.
examples.cn: 密封水样中没有发现任何微生物。

dict_mnemonic.text: micro-（微小）+ organism（生物体）→ 微小的生物体 → microorganism 微生物

root: 希腊 mikros「小」（阿提卡形式 smikros）→ 拉丁化前缀 micro- → 英语 micro- + organism（有机体，1825 年出现生物义）→ 1855 年合成 microorganism「微生物」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from scale to body plan, to taxonomy, to five habitats and roles: soil, sea, disease, use and indication.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从尺度走向身体构造，再走向分类，最后落到五种生境与角色：土壤、海洋、致病、利用与指示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of water under a lens, crowded with living shapes.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜片下的一滴水，挤满各种活的形状。

branches.en: SCALE AND BODY: smallness is the entry condition, and a single cell is the common body plan.
branches.cn: 尺度与身体：小是入门条件，单细胞是常见的身体构造。

branches.en: TAXONOMY: the class is defined by size, so it cuts across kingdoms and even touches the virus border.
branches.cn: 分类：这一类别按大小定义，因此横跨多个界，甚至触及病毒那条边界。

branches.en: HABITAT: the same word covers the decomposer in soil and the producer in the sea.
branches.cn: 生境：同一个词既涵盖土壤中的分解者，也涵盖海洋中的生产者。

branches.en: ROLE TOWARD HUMANS: one subset causes disease, another ferments food and makes medicine.
branches.cn: 对人的角色：一个子集致病，另一个子集发酵食物、制造药物。

branches.en: PROXY: an indicator microorganism is watched not for itself but for what its presence means.
branches.cn: 替身：监测指示微生物不是为了它本身，而是为了它的存在所意味的东西。

intro.en: Microorganism is a two-part scientific compound: a Greek prefix for smallness and a Greek-derived noun for a living body, joined in English.
intro.cn: microorganism 是两部分组成的科学复合词：表示「微小」的希腊前缀，加上希腊来源的「生物体」名词，在英语中组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Neither element is native Latin: micro- is the Latinized form of Greek mikros, and organismus is Modern/Medical Latin built on Greek organon. The compound itself was made in English, so no single Latin etymon exists.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是本族拉丁语：micro- 是希腊 mikros 的拉丁化形式，organismus 是建立在希腊 organon 上的现代或医学拉丁语。复合词本身在英语中构成，因此没有单一拉丁语词源。

items.meaning: a living thing visible only under a microscope
items.meaningCN: 只有借助显微镜才可见的生物
items.exampleCN: 一种微生物引发了这次水华。

items.example: The microbe was first seen in 1878.
items.exampleCN: 这种微生物最早于 1878 年被观察到。
微生物生命填满了这片菌席。
微生物学在 1880 年成为一门学科。
微生物学家培养了这份样本。

items.meaning: the microorganisms of a particular place
items.meaningCN: 某一特定地点的微生物群落
items.example: The gut microbiota changed with diet.
items.exampleCN: 肠道微生物群落随饮食而变。

items.meaning: the whole community and its genes
items.meaningCN: 整个微生物群落及其基因
items.example: The skin microbiome differs by site.
items.exampleCN: 皮肤微生物组因部位而异。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing small things
items.exampleCN: 显微镜使这些细胞显现出来。

latinEntries.structure: organismus, -i (m., Medical/Modern Latin, from Greek organon)

latinEntries.meaning: tool, instrument; organ of the body

definition_zh: 水圈；地球上全部水体的总称；行星的水层
definition_en: the whole body of water on a planet, including oceans, ice, groundwater, lakes, rivers and atmospheric vapour
core_image: 教室里的透明地球仪上，蓝色薄膜从海面一直裹到云底，薄得像一层漆
scene: 教室里摆着一只透明地球仪，蓝色薄膜从海面一直包到云层底部。 The hydrosphere includes the oceans, the ice caps, the groundwater and the water held in the air.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（地球上全部水体的总称）；句意为水圈包括海洋、冰盖、地下水以及悬浮在空气中的水。

pos.zh: 名词：水圈；地球全部水体；行星的水层

derivatives.zh: 由「水圈」加形容词词尾构成，义为「水圈的；水圈内的」
由希腊表示「水」的成分构成的构词成分，用于构成与水有关的术语
由希腊表示「球」的成分构成的构词成分，用于构成圈层名称

senses.title: All the water on Earth
senses.definition: the total mass of water on Earth, in every state and every reservoir
senses.definitionCN: 指地球上以各种状态存在于各处的全部水体
senses.example: The hydrosphere stores most of its water in the oceans.
senses.exampleCN: 水圈把大部分水储存在海洋里。
senses.why: The word names a sphere only because the total is imagined as one connected body.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把它称作「球」，只是因为人们把全部水量想象成一个连通的整体。

senses.title: The water shell of the planet
senses.definition: the water layer viewed as a shell surrounding the solid Earth
senses.definitionCN: 指把水看作包在固体地球外面的一层
senses.example: The hydrosphere forms a thin, broken shell around the planet.
senses.exampleCN: 水圈在地球外面形成一层薄而不连续的外壳。
senses.why: Earth-system science divides the planet into shells, and water is one of them.
senses.whyCN: 地球系统科学把行星分成若干圈层，水是其中之一。

senses.title: A subsystem of the Earth system
senses.definition: the water component that exchanges matter and energy with the atmosphere, lithosphere and biosphere
senses.definitionCN: 指与大气圈、岩石圈、生物圈交换物质与能量的水的部分
senses.example: Water moves constantly between the hydrosphere and the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 水在水圈与大气圈之间不断移动。
senses.why: Once the shell is treated as a system, its exchanges with neighbouring shells become the main story.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把这层当作系统，它与相邻圈层的交换就成了主要故事。

senses.title: A planet's water inventory
senses.definition: the water held by another planet or moon, whatever its state
senses.definitionCN: 指另一颗行星或卫星所拥有的水，不论其状态
senses.example: The Martian hydrosphere is now mostly frozen or buried.
senses.exampleCN: 火星的水圈如今大多冻结或埋在地下。
senses.why: Planetary scientists extended the terrestrial term to any world with water.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学家把地球上的这个术语扩展到任何有水的天体。

senses.title: The slow reservoir of the water cycle
senses.definition: the part of the water system that stores water for a long time, especially groundwater and ice
senses.definitionCN: 指水系统中长期储存水的部分，尤其是地下水与冰
senses.example: Groundwater is the slowest part of the hydrosphere to renew.
senses.exampleCN: 地下水是水圈中更新最慢的部分。
senses.why: Storage time separates a reservoir from a channel, and the phrase covers both.
senses.whyCN: 储存时间把储库与通道区分开来，而这条术语两者都包括。

senses.title: The freshwater share
senses.definition: the small fraction of the total that is fresh rather than saline
senses.definitionCN: 指总水量中非咸水的那一小部分
senses.example: Only a small fraction of the hydrosphere is fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 水圈中只有一小部分是淡水。
senses.why: The whole is mostly salt water, so the useful part needs a separate label.
senses.whyCN: 整体大多是咸水，因此有用的那一小部分需要一个单独的说法。

senses.title: Water as a managed resource
senses.definition: the water system considered as a resource to be measured, allocated and protected
senses.definitionCN: 指被计量、分配与保护的水系统
senses.example: Engineers treat the hydrosphere as a resource with limits.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把水圈当作有限资源来对待。
senses.why: Resource language shifts the focus from description to allocation.
senses.whyCN: 资源语言把重点从描述转向分配。

senses.title: The water of a closed local system
senses.definition: the water contained in an isolated body such as a lake, a cave or a sealed basin
senses.definitionCN: 指湖泊、洞穴或封闭盆地等孤立水体中所含的水
senses.example: The cave's hydrosphere is cut off from the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这个洞穴的水体与地表隔绝。
senses.why: The same word scales down to any bounded volume of water.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能缩小到任何有边界的水体。

intro.en: Hydrosphere joins Greek hydor, water, with Greek sphaira, a ball, through the Latin form sphaera. The compound was coined in the nineteenth century as a parallel to atmosphere and later lithosphere; the precise coinage date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语中表示「水」的词与表示「球」的词组合起来，后者经拉丁语形式进入欧洲语言。这个合成词在十九世纪仿照「大气圈」造出，后来又有了「岩石圈」等并列词；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Hydor meant water, and its stem supplies the first half of hydrology, hydrate and hydrosphere.
items.cn: 这个词意为水，其词干构成「水文学」「水合物」「水圈」等词的前半部分。

items.en: Sphaira meant a ball or a globe, the shape of a celestial body.
items.cn: 这个词意为球、球体，即天体的形状。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as sphaera, which passed into the European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词，后来又传入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English took the Latin noun for a round solid and later for any domain of activity.
items.cn: 英语借入这个拉丁名词，先指圆球体，后来指任何活动领域。

items.en: The compound was formed as a scientific parallel to atmosphere, naming the water shell of the planet.
items.cn: 这个合成词作为「大气圈」的科学类比而造，指地球的水层。

items.en: Twentieth-century Earth science made it one of several interacting shells, alongside atmosphere, lithosphere and biosphere.
items.cn: 二十世纪的地球科学把它与大气圈、岩石圈、生物圈并列，作为相互作用的圈层之一。

note.en: The first group shares the water or sphere element; the second group names neighbouring shells and water bodies.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「水」或「球」的成分；第二组是相邻圈层与具体水体的说法。

entries.definition: The air shell of a planet, coined with the same sphere element.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的空气层，用同一个「球」成分构成。

entries.definition: The rocky shell of a planet, built to match the water term.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的岩石层，按水的术语仿造。

entries.definition: The zone of life, another shell in the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 指生命存在的区域，同一族里的另一个圈层。

entries.definition: The scientific study of water, sharing the water root.
entries.definitionCN: 研究水的学科，共享「水」词根。

entries.definition: Half of a sphere, a word built with the same ball element.
entries.definitionCN: 指球的一半，用同一个「球」成分构成。

entries.definition: The circulation of water among ocean, air, land and life.
entries.definitionCN: 指水在海洋、大气、陆地与生物之间的循环。

entries.definition: An underground layer that stores and transmits groundwater.
entries.definitionCN: 指储存并输送地下水的地下岩层。

entries.definition: The area from which water drains into one river system.
entries.definitionCN: 指向同一河系汇水的区域。

entries.definition: A natural or artificial store of water.
entries.definitionCN: 指天然或人工的水储库。

entries.definition: The frozen part of the water system, ice and snow.
entries.definitionCN: 指水系统中冻结的部分，即冰与雪。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow water plus ball: a blue film wrapped around a globe.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「水」加「球」展开：一层裹住地球仪的蓝色薄膜。

normal.en: Water plus ball gives a water shell around a planet.
normal.cn: 水加球，就是行星外面的一层水壳。

normal.en: The ocean holds nearly all of it; ice, groundwater and vapour are the small shares.
normal.cn: 海洋占去几乎全部；冰、地下水与水汽只占小份。

normal.en: It sits beside atmosphere, lithosphere and biosphere in the same family of shells.
normal.cn: 它与大气圈、岩石圈、生物圈并列为同一族圈层。

normal.en: Groundwater is the slowest reservoir in the cycle.
normal.cn: 地下水是水循环中更新最慢的储库。

normal.en: Planetary scientists speak of a Martian hydrosphere, mostly frozen.
normal.cn: 行星科学家会说火星水圈，其中大部分已冻结。

abstract.en: A sphere is a way of seeing one connected thing where there are thousands of separate pools.
abstract.cn: 「球」是一种看法：把成千上万处分散的水看成一件连通的事。

abstract.en: Water is the part of a planet that keeps changing its address.
abstract.cn: 水是行星上不断更换住址的那一部分。

abstract.en: Every resource phrase begins as a description and ends as a budget.
abstract.cn: 每个资源说法都从描述开始，以预算告终。

examples.en: The hydrosphere exchanges heat with the atmosphere over every ocean surface.
examples.cn: 水圈在每一片海面上与大气圈交换热量。

examples.en: Most of the hydrosphere is salt water, so fresh water needs separate accounting.
examples.cn: 水圈的大部分是咸水，因此淡水需要单独核算。

examples.en: A planet's hydrosphere may be liquid, frozen or held as vapour.
examples.cn: 一颗行星的水圈可以是液态、冻结的，或以水汽形式存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「海德若斯菲尔」——海的水（海德）裹成一个球（斯菲尔），就是水圈：水圈、地球上的全部水体

root: 希腊语 hydor「水」加 sphaira「球」，后者经拉丁语 sphaera 进入欧洲语言；合成词于十九世纪仿「大气圈」造出，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat one blue film as total water, as a shell, as a system, as a planet's inventory, as storage, as freshwater, as a resource and as a sealed local pool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一层蓝色薄膜分别看作全部水量、一个圈层、一个系统、一颗行星的水量、储库、淡水、资源，以及局部封闭的水体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blue skin over a classroom globe, running from sea surface to cloud base.
core.cn: 核心意象：教室地球仪上的一层蓝色薄皮，从海面一直铺到云底。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND THE SHELL: all water at once, imagined as a layer around the solid Earth.
branches.cn: 整体与外壳：一次性看全部水，把它想象成包住固体地球的一层。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: water exchanging matter and energy with air, rock and life.
branches.cn: 系统：水与空气、岩石、生命交换物质与能量。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the same term extended to any planet's water.
branches.cn: 别的世界：同一术语扩展到任何行星的水。

branches.en: STORAGE AND THE USEFUL PART: slow reservoirs, and the small fresh fraction.
branches.cn: 储存与可用部分：缓慢的储库，以及那一小份淡水。

branches.en: FROM BUDGET TO BOUNDARY: water allocated as a resource, and water sealed inside a local body.
branches.cn: 从预算到边界：作为资源分配的水，以及封闭在局部水体中的水。

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound wearing a Latinised sphere; both halves are transparent and productive.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊合成词，只把「球」写成了拉丁化形式；两半都清楚且能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the form of the sphere word; the water element is Greek and has no native Latin root here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「球」这个词的书写形式；「水」的成分出自希腊语，此处没有本土拉丁词根。

items.example: It is the first element of hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它是「水圈」的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the second element of hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它是「水圈」的第二个成分。

items.example: Latin passed the form to later European languages.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形式传给后来的欧洲语言。

items.example: English uses it for both shapes and fields.
items.exampleCN: 英语用它指形状，也指领域。

items.example: It builds atmosphere, biosphere and hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「大气圈」「生物圈」「水圈」等词。

items.example: It builds hydrology, hydroelectric and hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「水文学」「水电」「水圈」等词。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin-derived ending to the compound.
items.exampleCN: 形容词给合成词加了源自拉丁语的词尾。

items.example: It is the Latin word for water, used in aquifer and aquatic.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语中表示「水」的词，用于「含水层」「水生」等词。

items.example: It is built on the same pattern with a Greek word for cold.
items.exampleCN: 它按同一模式加希腊语表示「寒冷」的词构成。

derivatives.zh: 由「水圈」加形容词词尾构成，义为「水圈的」
由希腊「水」成分构成的构词成分，用于构成与水有关的术语
由希腊「球」成分构成的构词成分，用于构成圈层名称
按同一模式由「寒冷」加「圈层」构成，义为「冰冻圈」

definition_zh: 冶金的；冶金学的：与从矿石提取金属、精炼金属，或与金属内部组织及性能相关的
definition_en: relating to metallurgy, or to the extraction, refining and internal study of metals
core_image: 显微镜下的一小片抛光金属，深浅不一的晶粒被清晰的边界分开
scene: 试样抛光后在显微镜下显出深浅不一的晶粒，工程师据此判断这一炉是否合格。 A metallurgical problem in the alloy delayed the whole shipment.
sceneCN: 这里指与金属内部组织有关的（第 3 个义项：属于物理冶金的、关于金属组织的）；句意为合金上出现的一个冶金问题拖住了整批发货。

pos.zh: 冶金的；冶金学的（用于修饰工艺、性质、行业、人员等）

collocations.zh: 炼焦煤（用于冶金的煤种）
由冶金原因导致的失效

forms.label: 比较级（少见，非通常可分级）

derivatives.zh: metallurgical + -ly（副词后缀）→ 从冶金角度看，语义偏移为「在冶金工艺层面上」
metallurgical 的名词基础，来自希腊 metallon + ergon → 冶金学；形容词与名词同族
non-（非）+ metallurgical → 非冶金的，语义偏移为「不属于冶金环节的」
pyro-（火）+ metallurgical → 火法冶金的，语义偏移为「靠高温处理的」
hydro-（水）+ metallurgical → 湿法冶金的，语义偏移为「用溶液处理的」

senses.title: Of the discipline
senses.titleCN: 学科属性：属于冶金学的
senses.definition: belonging to metallurgy as a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为一门学问的冶金学
senses.example: Metallurgical research at the institute focuses on phase diagrams.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究所的冶金研究以相图为主。
senses.why: The -ical ending makes a relational adjective: it does not mean 'metal' but 'of the field that studies metal', so it points at the discipline rather than at the material.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词后缀构成关系形容词：它不是「金属的」，而是「研究金属那门学问的」，指向学科而非材料。

senses.title: Of winning metal
senses.titleCN: 提取与精炼：属于把金属从矿石中取出的环节
senses.definition: relating to the extraction and refining of metal from ore
senses.definitionCN: 与从矿石中提取、精炼金属有关的
senses.example: The metallurgical process begins with roasting the concentrate.
senses.exampleCN: 这一冶金过程从焙烧精矿开始。
senses.why: In a works the adjective marks the front half of the chain, where rock is still being turned into metal; the shaping of the finished metal comes later and belongs to other trades.
senses.whyCN: 在厂里，这个形容词标出链条的前半段——石头还在变成金属；成品金属的成形属于后面的行当。

senses.title: Of the metal's inside
senses.titleCN: 组织与性能：属于物理冶金的
senses.definition: relating to the internal structure of a metal and the properties that structure produces
senses.definitionCN: 与金属内部组织以及由该组织决定的性能有关的
senses.example: A metallurgical microscope revealed unusually large grains.
senses.exampleCN: 金相显微镜显示晶粒异常粗大。
senses.why: Once a metal exists, the question shifts from where it came from to how its grains are arranged; the same adjective now points inward at structure.
senses.whyCN: 金属一旦存在，问题就从「它从哪里来」转向「它的晶粒怎样排列」；同一个形容词此时向内指向组织。

senses.title: Of a grade
senses.titleCN: 等级属性：冶金级的原料或产品
senses.definition: used of raw materials or products graded for use in metal production
senses.definitionCN: 用于标明供金属生产使用的原料或产品等级
senses.example: Metallurgical coal must be low in ash and sulphur.
senses.exampleCN: 炼焦煤必须低灰低硫。
senses.why: Some materials exist only to feed a furnace, so a whole grade of coal or coke is named by the industry it serves rather than by what it is.
senses.whyCN: 有些材料存在的唯一目的就是进炉，于是整整一个煤或焦的等级，是按它服务的行业来命名的，而不是按它本身是什么。

senses.title: Of a cause of failure
senses.titleCN: 失效归因：由冶金原因造成的
senses.definition: describing a failure whose cause lies in the metal's composition, structure or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 描述原因出在金属成分、组织或处理上的失效
senses.example: The crack was a metallurgical failure, not a design fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裂纹属于冶金失效，而不是设计缺陷。
senses.why: When a part breaks, engineers sort causes by stage; if the fault was already in the metal before it was shaped, the failure is labelled with this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 零件断裂时，工程师按阶段给原因归类；如果毛病在成形之前就已藏在金属里，这类失效就用这个形容词来标记。

senses.title: Of the industry
senses.titleCN: 产业属性：冶金工业与工厂
senses.definition: belonging to the industry, its plants and its equipment
senses.definitionCN: 属于冶金工业、其工厂与设备的
senses.example: The metallurgical industry employs thousands in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 冶金工业在这个山谷里雇用了数千人。
senses.why: An adjective can name a whole sector by its core activity, and then attach itself to plants, towns and jobs that live off that activity.
senses.whyCN: 一个形容词可以用核心活动来命名整个部门，再附着到靠这项活动生存的工厂、城镇与岗位上。

senses.title: Of people and teaching
senses.titleCN: 人员、教学与文献：属于冶金专业的
senses.definition: used of metallurgical engineers, courses, journals and textbooks
senses.definitionCN: 用于冶金工程师、课程、期刊与教科书
senses.example: She wrote the standard metallurgical textbook on copper smelting.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了那本关于炼铜的标准冶金教科书。
senses.why: A field trains its own people and writes its own books; the adjective travels with them, marking what belongs to the profession rather than to the metal.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问会培养自己的人、写自己的书；这个形容词随他们一起走，标出属于这一行而非属于金属本身的东西。

senses.title: Of testing old metal
senses.titleCN: 检验属性：用于对金属器物的科学分析
senses.definition: used of the scientific examination of metal objects, especially in archaeology and conservation
senses.definitionCN: 用于对金属器物进行的科学检验，尤在考古与文物保护中
senses.example: Metallurgical analysis showed the pin was almost pure copper.
senses.exampleCN: 冶金分析显示这枚别针几乎是纯铜。
senses.why: A museum object cannot be re-smelted, so the only way to know its metal is to measure it; the adjective marks the laboratory half of that work.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆的器物不能再熔一次，唯一知道它是什么金属的办法就是测量；这个形容词标出这项工作里属于实验室的那一半。

intro.en: Metallurgical is the adjective of metallurgy, built from a Greek compound plus a Latin adjectival ending. The Greek first element remains the uncertain part.
intro.cn: metallurgical 是 metallurgy 的形容词，由希腊复合词加拉丁形容词词尾构成。希腊语的第一个成分仍是存疑之处。

items.en: Metallon 'metal, mine' and ergon 'work' formed metallourgia, the working of metals. Metallon's own origin is uncertain, and the ancient link to metalleuein 'to mine' is an explanation rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: metallon「金属、矿」与 ergon「劳作」构成 metallourgia，即金属的加工。metallon 自身的来源不确定，古人把它与 metalleuein「采矿」相联系，那是一种解释而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Latin formed the adjective metallurgicus on the model of metallurgia, alongside metallicus 'of metal'. The two adjectives were kept apart: one belonged to the craft, the other to the material.
items.cn: 拉丁语依照 metallurgia 造出形容词 metallurgicus，同时另有 metallicus「金属的」。两个形容词彼此分工：一个属于工艺，一个属于材料。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin adjective and reshaped it with -ical, the ending that makes relational adjectives such as metallurgical, chemical and practical.
items.cn: 英语借入拉丁形容词后，用 -ical 这一词尾重塑，它正是构成 metallurgical、chemical、practical 这类关系形容词的后缀。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective attached itself to processes, grades, microscopes and failures, until metallurgical became a general label for anything belonging to the industrial handling of metal.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词附着到工艺、等级、显微镜与失效上，逐渐成为任何与金属工业处理有关之物的通称。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest English use is not precisely dated, metallon has no agreed etymology, and every proposed Indo-European source for either Greek element is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最早的英语用例没有精确年代，metallon 没有公认词源，凡为两个希腊成分拟出的印欧来源都是重构。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the same family from near neighbours; group two separates words about metal as a material from words about working it.
note.cn: 第一组把同族形式与邻近词分开；第二组把指金属材料的词与指加工金属的词分开。

entries.definition: The field itself. The adjective describes something belonging to it; the noun names it.
entries.definitionCN: 这门学问本身。形容词描述属于它的东西，名词则是它的名称。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective with the same sense, built with -ic instead of -ical; the longer form is the usual one.
entries.definitionCN: 意义相同但少见的形容词，用 -ic 而非 -ical 构成；较长的那一种是常用形式。

entries.definition: An element between metals and non-metals. The -oid ending means 'like', so it is not an adjective of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 介于金属与非金属之间的元素。-oid 词尾意为「像」，因此它不是本学科的形容词。

entries.definition: The practitioner. It ends in -ist, which marks a person, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 从业者。它以 -ist 结尾，标记的是人，而不是属性。

entries.definition: Made of metal, or resembling metal in shine or sound; it describes the material itself, not the science of winning it.
entries.definitionCN: 金属制的，或在光泽与声音上像金属的；它描述材料本身，而不是提取它的学问。

entries.definition: Containing metal, said of rock or ore; it is a statement about the ground, not about a process.
entries.definitionCN: 含金属的，用于岩石或矿石；它说的是地层，而不是工艺。

entries.definition: The shaping and joining of metal after it has been refined; metallurgical work begins earlier, at the ore.
entries.definitionCN: 金属精炼之后的成形与连接；冶金工作开始得更早，从矿石就开始了。

entries.definition: The broader study of all materials, of which the metallurgical branch is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 研究所有材料的更大学科，冶金分支只是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Greek elements, the Latin adjective, and the fixed phrases that mark each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个希腊成分、拉丁形容词，以及标出各义项的固定搭配。

normal.en: metallon 'metal' + ergon 'work' + -ical: literally 'of the metal-working'. The whole adjective is readable from its parts.
normal.cn: metallon「金属」+ ergon「劳作」+ -ical：字面就是「属于金属加工的」。整个形容词可由各部分读出。

normal.en: The ending -ical makes a relation, not a substance: metallurgical research is research in the field, not research on metal alone.
normal.cn: -ical 词尾造出的是关系而非物质：冶金研究是在这门学问里做研究，而不只是研究金属。

normal.en: The neighbours sort themselves: metallurgy is the field, metallurgist the person, metallurgical the property of belonging to it.
normal.cn: 同族词各就各位：metallurgy 是学问，metallurgist 是从业者，metallurgical 是属于这门学问的属性。

normal.en: Its fixed phrases mark the stages: metallurgical process, metallurgical coal, metallurgical microscope, metallurgical failure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各个阶段：冶金过程、炼焦煤、金相显微镜、冶金失效。

normal.en: The microscope is the giveaway: if the adjective is used with a lens, it points at structure rather than at ore.
normal.cn: 显微镜是个提示：当这个形容词与镜头一起出现，它指的是组织，而不是矿石。

abstract.en: Picture the adjective as a label pinned to a chain of stages, moving from rock to ingot to grain to broken part.
abstract.cn: 想象这个形容词是一枚标签，别在一条阶段链上：从石头到铸锭，到晶粒，再到断掉的零件。

abstract.en: Picture a metal's inside as a map of small territories, each boundary a place where cracks can start.
abstract.cn: 想象金属内部是一张小区划图，每条边界都是裂纹可能起步的地方。

abstract.en: Picture the word as a lens: it never looks at the metal from outside, only at what belongs to the craft that handles it.
abstract.cn: 想象这个词是一片透镜：它从不从外面看金属，只看属于处理金属那门手艺的东西。

examples.en: Metallurgical coke is produced in ovens that must be kept at a steady heat.
examples.cn: 冶金焦是在必须保持稳定温度的火炉中生产的。

examples.en: The report blamed a metallurgical defect rather than the welding.
examples.cn: 报告把问题归因于冶金缺陷，而不是焊接。

examples.en: Her metallurgical training let her read the slag like a page of history.
examples.cn: 她的冶金训练让她能把炉渣当作一页历史来读。

dict_mnemonic.text: metall（金属）+ urg（劳作）+ ical（形容词）＝ 金属加工的；记「炉前提取、镜后看晶粒」。

root: 希腊 metallon「金属、矿」+ ergon「劳作」→ metallourgia，拉丁形容词 metallurgicus，英语加 -ical；metallon 来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight adjective senses travel along the metal chain: the field, the ore, the grain, the grade, the failure, the industry, the people, and the museum test.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个形容词义项沿着金属链移动：学问、矿石、晶粒、等级、失效、产业、人员，最后是对器物的检验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lens on polished metal, where bright grains meet along dark boundaries.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片抛光金属在镜头下，明亮的晶粒沿着暗色边界相接。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the adjective marks what belongs to the discipline itself.
branches.cn: 学问层：这个形容词标出属于学科本身的东西。

branches.en: THE FRONT OF THE CHAIN: extraction and refining, where rock becomes metal.
branches.cn: 链条前端：提取与精炼，石头在这里变成金属。

branches.en: THE INSIDE: grains and boundaries, seen in a works or measured in a museum.
branches.cn: 内部层：晶粒与边界，或在厂里被看见，或在博物馆里被测量。

branches.en: THE SCALE OF INDUSTRY: a graded raw material and a sector with plants and jobs.
branches.cn: 产业尺度：一种被定级的原料，以及拥有工厂与岗位的整个部门。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THE BREAK: engineers and textbooks on one side, failures blamed on the metal on the other.
branches.cn: 人与断裂：一边是工程师与教科书，另一边是归咎于金属的失效。

intro.en: The adjective combines a Greek noun root, a Greek work root and a Latin-derived English ending; each piece is still productive.
intro.cn: 这个形容词组合了希腊名词词根、希腊「劳作」词根，以及源自拉丁的英语词尾；每一部分至今都能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied metallum for the material, metallurgia for the craft and metallurgicus for the adjective; English took the last two through learned and technical writing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了指材料的 metallum、指工艺的 metallurgia，以及形容词 metallurgicus；英语经学术与技术文献吸收了后两者。

items.example: The metallo- prefix also opens metallocene.
Dramaturgy uses the same work element.
items.exampleCN: dramaturgy 用了同一个「劳作」成分。

items.example: The same ending builds chemical and practical.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 chemical 与 practical。

items.meaning: the craft of winning and preparing metals
items.meaningCN: 提取与处理金属的工艺
items.example: Metallurgy is the noun behind this adjective.
items.exampleCN: metallurgy 是这个形容词背后的名词。

items.meaning: a person who practises the craft
items.example: A metallurgist checked the furnace lining.
items.exampleCN: 一位冶金学家检查了炉衬。

items.meaning: in metallurgical terms; as regards the metal
items.meaningCN: 从冶金角度看；就金属而言
items.example: The two ores are metallurgically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种矿石在冶金性质上相似。

items.example: The pyrometallurgical route consumes less water.
items.exampleCN: 火法冶金路线耗水更少。

items.example: The hydrometallurgical plant leaches copper from heaps.
items.exampleCN: 湿法冶金厂从矿堆中浸出铜。

items.example: Nonmetallurgical uses of the coke include heating.
items.exampleCN: 这种焦炭的非冶金用途包括取暖。

latinEntries.structure: metallum, -i (n., second declension, from Greek metallon)

definition_zh: v. 扩散；传播；散布；使弥漫 adj. 弥散的；分散的；冗长啰嗦的
definition_en: to spread or send out widely through a space or among people; as an adjective, spread thin or long-winded
core_image: 一滴墨落进清水，颜色向四周丝丝散开；同一瓶香水的气味慢慢填满整间屋子
scene: 香气在屋里慢慢散开。 The scent begins to diffuse through the room.
sceneCN: 这里 diffuse 是动词，指气味充满一个空间（第 3 个义项：使光或气味弥漫）；句意是香气在屋里慢慢散开。图中可辨识物件：敞口的香瓶、飘散的细线、房间的门框。

pos.zh: 弥散的；分散的；冗长啰嗦的

senses.title: Spread through a medium
senses.definition: of particles, to mix through a gas or liquid by their own motion
senses.definitionCN: （动词）颗粒靠自身运动在气体或液体中混合开来
senses.example: The dye diffuses slowly through the water.
senses.exampleCN: 染料在水里慢慢扩散。
senses.why: A drop of ink opening into threads inside a glass of clear water.
senses.whyCN: 一滴墨在一杯清水里散成丝缕。

senses.title: Send out among people
senses.definition: to circulate ideas or news widely among many people
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把观念或消息广泛传到许多人中间
senses.example: Schools diffuse knowledge beyond the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把知识传播到课堂之外。
senses.why: A notice copied and handed from one desk to the next.
senses.whyCN: 一张通知被复印后从一张桌子传到下一张。

senses.title: Fill a space
senses.definition: to make light or a smell spread through a whole space
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让光或气味充满整个空间
senses.example: The scent begins to diffuse through the room.
senses.exampleCN: 香气在屋里慢慢散开。
senses.why: An open perfume bottle with faint lines drifting to the doorframe.
senses.whyCN: 一只敞口的香水瓶，细线般的气味飘向门框。

senses.title: Not concentrated
senses.definition: spread over a wide area rather than gathered in one place
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）铺开在大范围而非集中在一处
senses.example: The city has a diffuse pattern of small workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的作坊分布很分散。
senses.why: Many tiny dots scattered across a map instead of one blob.
senses.whyCN: 地图上许多小点散开，而不是聚成一团。

senses.title: Wordy and rambling
senses.definition: of speech or writing, long and loosely organised
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）（言语或文章）冗长而组织松散
senses.example: His argument was diffuse and hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 他的论证冗长散漫，难以跟上。
senses.why: A paragraph whose sentences wander past every margin.
senses.whyCN: 一段文字的句子越过每一道页边四处游荡。

intro.en: Diffuse comes from Latin diffundere, from dis- apart and fundere to pour; its past participle diffusus gave both the verb and the adjective.
intro.cn: diffuse 来自拉丁语 diffundere，由 dis-（分开）与 fundere（倾倒）构成；其过去分词 diffusus 同时给出了动词与形容词。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾倒。

items.en: Dis- meant apart or in different directions.
items.cn: dis- 意为分开、朝不同方向。

items.en: Diffundere meant to pour out widely.
items.cn: diffundere 意为四处倾泻、泼洒开来。

items.en: Diffusus, the past participle, meant spread out.
items.cn: 过去分词 diffusus 意为铺展开的。

items.en: Diffuse entered English for spreading abroad.
items.cn: 十五世纪 diffuse 以向外散布义进入英语。

items.en: Science used diffusion for particles mixing by themselves.
items.cn: 科学界用 diffusion 指颗粒自行混合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fuse spelling, and defuse is the classic trap; the near-meaning group names other ways of spreading.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fuse 的拼写，其中 defuse 是最经典的陷阱；近义组是其他表示「散开」的词。

entries.definition: To remove a fuse or calm a tense situation, not to spread.
entries.definitionCN: 拆掉引信或缓和紧张局势，不是「扩散」。

entries.definition: To pour together so things become unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 倒在一起使事情变得不清。

entries.definition: To pour a quality or liquid into something.
entries.definitionCN: 把某种性质或液体注入其中。

entries.definition: To break up and go in different directions.
entries.definitionCN: 分散开来朝不同方向去。

entries.definition: To extend over a larger area.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展到更大的范围。

entries.definition: Long and wandering without a clear order.
entries.definitionCN: 冗长散漫、缺乏条理。

normalIntro.en: Diffuse is dis- apart plus fuse pour: pour it in every direction, and mind the defuse trap.
normalIntro.cn: diffuse 就是 dis-（分开）加 fuse（倒）：往每个方向倒出去；小心 defuse 这个陷阱。

normal.en: Dis- apart plus fuse pour means pour it apart.
normal.cn: dis-（分开）加 fuse（倒）就是往四处倒。

normal.en: The verb ends in a z sound, the adjective in an s sound.
normal.cn: 动词末尾读 z 音，形容词末尾读 s 音。

normal.en: You diffuse a scent but defuse a bomb.
normal.cn: 气味用 diffuse，炸弹用 defuse。

normal.en: Diffusion is the noun, diffusive the adjective.
normal.cn: diffusion 是名词，diffusive 是形容词。

normal.en: A diffuse essay pours words in every direction.
normal.cn: 一篇冗长的文章把词句往各个方向倒。

dict_mnemonic.text: diffuse ＝ dif-（＝dis-，分开）＋ fuse（拉丁语 fundere「倾倒」，同根 confuse、infuse、profuse）＝往四处倒出去，「扩散、传播」；形容词指「弥散的、冗长的」。别和 defuse（拆引信、缓和）混。

root: 拉丁语 dis-（分开）＋ fundere（倾倒）→ diffundere（四处倾泻）→ 过去分词 diffusus → 英语 diffuse

sensesIntro.en: One drop poured in every direction: ink in water, news in a town and a sentence that will not stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 一滴往每个方向倒出去的东西：水里的墨、镇上的消息，以及一句停不下来的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink poured into clear water and opening outward in every direction at once
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴墨倒进清水，同时朝每个方向向外散开

intro.cn: diffuse 由 dif- 加 fus- 构成；倾倒这个词根也造出 confuse、infuse、profuse 与 effusive。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere means to pour, diffusus spread out and spargere to scatter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundere 意为倾倒，diffusus 意为铺展开的，spargere 意为撒开。
